name: Abucay
summary: Abucay is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. Situated at the eastern side of the Bataan peninsula, it has natural and historic attractions, including the oldest Roman Catholic church in Bataan.

name: Abulug
summary: Abulug is a coastal municipality in Cagayan on Luzon, the Philippines. It is the main population hub and commercial center of northwestern Cagayan and the main point of entry into much of Apayao province.

name: Abuyog
summary: Abuyog is a municipality in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Aglipay
summary: Aglipay is a municipality in Quirino.

name: Agoo
summary: Agoo (pronounced as “Ago-o”) is a town in La Union. It has extensive beaches, a nature reserve and a Roman Catholic pilgrimage site and is one of the main entryways to Baguio.

name: Aklan
summary: Aklan is the oldest province in the Philippines dated since 1213 AD. It is located in the northwestern part of Panay Island in the Western Visayas Region. This province is the home of the country's version of Mardi Gras Ati-Atihan Festival.

name: Alaminos
summary: Alaminos City is a vibrant city in Pangasinan, with a growing tourism industry, largely attributed to the natural beauty of the Hundred Islands National Park.

name: Alaminos (Laguna)
summary: Alaminos is a small town in the province of Laguna.

name: Albay
summary: Albay (pronunciation: ahll-BIGH) is a province in the Bicol Region in the island of Luzon, Philippines. It is bordered by the provinces of Camarines Sur in the north and Sorsogon in the south. Its main draw is the active Mayon Volcano, an almost perfect cone-shaped volcano where the province is best known for. A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, it blends natural wonders with rich Bicolano culture, cuisine, and adventure.

name: Alcala
summary: Alcala (Pangasinan: Baley na Alcala; Ilocano: Ili ti Alcala; Tagalog: Bayan ng Alcala) is a 3rd class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. In 2020, it has a population of 49,000 people.

name: Alegria (Cebu)
summary: Alegria is a quiet coastal municipality in southwestern Cebu known for dramatic limestone cliffs, turquoise waters, canyon adventures, and a slower pace compared to the heavily commercialized tourism centers farther north. While many travelers pass through on the way to Moalboal or Badian, Alegria has gradually emerged as a destination in its own right — especially for canyoneering, waterfalls, and rural eco-tourism.

name: Alfonso Castañeda
summary: Alfonso Castañeda is a town in southern Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated at the headwaters of the Cagayan and Pampanga Rivers and the junction of two mountain ranges, it forms the lever in the pan-shaped province and has multiple natural attractions and indigenous tribes.

name: Alona Beach
summary: Alona Beach is on Panglao Island in Bohol province, Philippines. It is both the island and the province's most popular resort area, and one of the top ones for the country as a whole.

name: Altavas
summary: Altavas is a 4th class municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Anda
summary: Anda is a town on the east side of Bohol with one of the nicest beaches in all of the Philippine islands with access to a toilet and a decent cup of coffee.

name: Angeles
summary: Angeles is a city in Pampanga province. The city is rich in history and heritage, with old and historical significant buildings dotting its landscape, but these days it is best known for its high concentration of casinos and sometimes questionable nightlife (though that's changing; see "Drink" below). Aside from these, it is also famous for its extreme sports adventures in the lahar flows of Mt. Pinatubo.

name: Angono
summary: Angono (pronounced as “ah-NGAW-naw”) is a town in Rizal, Philippines. Now part of Manila's ever-expanding sprawl, , but it keeps its small town feel; most visitors will be drawn by its annual Higantes Festival, where papier-mache effigies are paraded around the town. Home to two renowned Filipino artists, the town is promoted as the "Art Capital of the Philippines"

name: Antipolo
summary: Antipolo is a highland city and the capital of the province of Rizal, Philippines. Sitting above a plateau above sea level, Antipolo is a respite from Manila's chaos, allowing a scenic view of an otherwise crowded and bustling metropolis.

name: Antique
summary: Antique is a province on the island of Panay in the Philippines.

name: Apalit
summary: Apalit is a municipality in the province of Pampanga, Philippines. It is a primarily commercial town at the crossroads between the Pampanga River delta, Bulacan, and the rest of Pampanga.

name: Aparri
summary: Aparri is a town in northern Cagayan. It lies at the mouth of the Cagayan River which drains into the Babuyan Channel. This article covers only the mainland portion; Fuga Island, while administratively part of the town, is considered a separate destination.

name: Apayao
summary: Apayao is a province in the Cordillera region of Luzon in the Philippines. One of the country's least-known provinces and the Cordillera's "Last Frontier", it has underrated natural and cultural attractions such as indigenous villages and unspoiled, jungle-covered mountains.

name: Apo Island
summary: Apo Island is in the province of Negros Oriental, in the Central Visayas region of the Philippines, about 30 km (20 miles) south of the provincial capital of Dumaguete. Administratively, the island is a barangay of the town of Dauin; population is about a thousand.

name: Arayat
summary: Arayat is a town in northern Pampanga, Philippines. It is named after the eponymous inactive volcano that looms over it.

name: Argao
summary: Argao is a town on Cebu Island, south of Metro Cebu.

name: Aringay
summary: Aringay (pronounced uh-ring-guy) is a town in La Union.

name: Atimonan
summary: Atimonan is a rural municipality, the gateway to eastern Quezon.

name: Atok
summary: Atok is a municipality in the province of Benguet, Philippines.

name: Aurora (province)
summary: Aurora is a coastal province of Central Luzon region in the Philippines. Little is known about the province due to its remoteness, but its capital is known for its surfing scene, and the province has one of the largest expanses of rainforest spared from development, and also has hidden beaches and mountains.

name: Baao
summary: Baao is a municipality in Rinconada District of Camarines Sur.

name: Babatngon
summary: Babatngon is a town of 29,000 people (2020) in the northern part of the island of Leyte, Philippines, along the shore of Carigara Bay. Babatngon is known for Busay Falls, a three-tiered cataract which is an attraction for picnickers who flock to Babatngon during the summer months. A massive bowl of solid, moss-covered rock catches the cool waters of the third fall.

name: Babuyan and Calayan Islands
summary: The Babuyan and Calayan Islands are a volcanic archipelago in the Babuyan Channel between northern Luzon and Batanes that belong to the province of Cagayan in northern Philippines. It it is comprised of five major islands, four of which (Babuyan, Calayan, Dalupiri, and Camiguin) are administered by the municipality of Calayan, while the island of Fuga is administratively part of Aparri.

name: Bacacay
summary: Bacacay is a municipality in the east coast of Albay accessible via Legazpi-Tiwi coastal road and has a shoreline facing both Lagonoy Gulf and Albay Gulf. Separates the municipalities of Santo Domingo and Malilipot, it is a fishing town with beaches, islands and caves.

name: Bacarra
summary: Bacarra is a town in Ilocos Norte. It is famous for its leaning, albeit partially ruined belltower.

name: Baclayon
summary: The historic town of Baclayon lies 6 km east along the seashore from Tagbilaran city on the Visayan island of Bohol in the Philippines. It was the first town established in Bohol by the Spaniards. Its 16th-century church, the pier and harbor it overlooks, and the elegant and well-preserved heritage houses lining the roads, make the township a charming and idyllic destination.

name: Bacnotan
summary: Bacnotan is a coastal town in La Union.

name: Baco
summary: Baco a municipality in Oriental Mindoro. It's a quiet place, out of the way of the bustling night-life and commerce of Puerto Galera and Sabang, 45 minutes to the west (by jeepney), and the uninteresting capital of Calapan, 30 minutes to the east.

name: Bacolod
summary: Bacolod is the capital of the province of Negros Occidental in the Philippines and the most populous city on Negros Island. It is known for its MassKara Festival, a Mardi Gras-like parade and spectacular mix of dancing, colour and music held every October, as well as for its culinary heritage that includes inasal (a kind of roast chicken on skewers) and sweet dessert treats.

name: Bacolor
summary: Bacolor is a town in Pampanga, the Philippines. Formerly the provincial capital, it was devastated by lahar flows from the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo but has since recovered with the help of renewed interest in its ruined state.

name: Bacoor
summary: Bacoor (pronounced “Ba-ko-or”) is a suburban city in Cavite. It is a large, overwhelmingly sprawling community south of Manila, and the gateway to the province from the north.

name: Badian
summary: Badian is a municipality on the southwest coast of Cebu Island.

name: Badoc
summary: Badoc is a town in Ilocos Norte. Situated at the boundary with Ilocos Sur province, it is famous for being the birthplace of two of the Philippines' national heroes, and is a pilgrimage spot for one of the most venerated images of the Virgin Mary in the Ilocos Region.

name: Bagabag
summary: Bagabag is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated at northern edge of the Magat River Valley, it is the main point of entry leading to Ifugao and Isabela provinces.

name: Bagac
summary: Bagac is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. It is a resort town famous for its beaches and Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar, a collection of colonial-era residences and buildings from the Spanish era.

name: Baggao
summary: Baggao (pronounced “Bug-gao”) is a town of Cagayan province in the Philippines. It is home to multiple natural attractions along the Sierra Madre mountains.

name: Bago (Philippines)
summary: Bago City is a city in Negros Occidental. It is known for its historical sites and natural treasures, and as the "rice granary of Negros Occidental".

name: Baguio
summary: Baguio is a highland city of 366,358 people (2020 census) in the province of Benguet, Philippines. Due to its cool mountain weather relative to the rest of the country, it is considered the "Summer Capital of the Philippines." The city is abundant in pine trees, so it is nicknamed the City of Pines.

name: Bagulin
summary: Bagulin is a town in La Union.

name: Bais
summary: Bais City is one of the cleanest and safest cities of the Philippines in Negros Oriental province. The main tourist draw is whale and dolphin watching in the Tañon Strait between Bais and the neighbouring island of Cebu.

name: Balabac
summary: Balabac is a second-class municipality in the southern tip of Palawan consisting of 32 islands. Being the westernmost point of the country, it is closer to Sabah than the rest of the Philippines, with only the Sabah Strait separating the municipality from its neighboring country.

name: Balanga (Bataan)
summary: Balanga is the provincial capital and the only city in Bataan.

name: Balaoan
summary: Balaoan is a town in La Union. It has extensive beaches and a Spanish-era watchtower.

name: Balayan
summary: Balayan is a municipality, the traditional commercial center of the western part of Batangas.

name: Baler
summary: Baler is the capital of Aurora Province on the east coast of Luzon in the Philippines. It is situated between the Sierra Madre mountain range and the Pacific Ocean, in the vast plain at the mouth of Baler Bay. For practical reasons, the guide includes the neighboring municipalities of Maria Aurora and San Luis, which form a loose urban conurbation around Baler.

name: Baliwag
summary: Baliwag, sometimes written as Baliuag, is a city and the largest settlement in northern Bulacan.

name: Bamban
summary: Bamban is a town in southern Tarlac.

name: Bambang
summary: Bambang is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. It is one of the three main economic centers of the province along with Solano and Bayombong.

name: Banaue
summary: Banaue is a town in the province of Ifugao in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. It is mainly visited for its stunning rice terraces, which are designated a National Cultural Treasure.

name: Bangar (La Union)
summary:
For the town in Brunei, see Bangar.
Bangar (pronounced buhng-gar) is a town in La Union.

name: Bangsamoro
summary: Bangsamoro, or Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in full, is a Muslim-dominant region of Mindanao. The region once formed the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM), renamed after a plebiscite in January 2019.

name: Bangui (Ilocos Norte)
summary: Bangui (pronounced bang-GEE) is a municipality in the far northern end of the province of Ilocos Norte in the Philippines. It is primarily known for its wind turbines that face the coast.

name: Bantayan
summary: Bantayan is an island that is part of Cebu Province.

name: Baras
summary: Baras is a town in Rizal, Philippines.

name: Basay (Negros Oriental)
summary: Basay is the westernmost town on the south coast of Negros Oriental, right at the border with Negros Occidental. Population was about 25,000 as of the 2010 census.

name: Basco
summary: Basco is the provincial capital of the smallest Philippine province, Batanes. It is on Batan Island.

name: Basey
summary: Basey is a municipality in Samar Province, Eastern Visayas, Philippines. Basey is famous for its beautiful Sohoton Caves, whose inner chamber features stalactites, stalagmites, and an underground river. The town is also known for artistically woven decorative mats called Banig.

name: Basilan
summary: Basilan is an island province of the Philippines in Mindanao, just off the southern coast of the Zamboanga Peninsula. Basilan is the biggest and northernmost among the major islands of the Sulu Archipelago.

name: Bataan
summary: Bataan is a province at the Central Luzon region of Luzon. A peninsula surrounded by Manila Bay to the east and the West Philippine Sea (or South China Sea) to the west, it is known in history as the last stronghold of the Americans in the Philippines when the Japanese invaded it during World War II.

name: Batac
summary: Batac is a city of over 55,000 in Ilocos Norte. It is known for being the home of the Aglipayan Church, a nationalist splinter sect from the Roman Catholic Church, and the Marcos political family, which has produced two Philippine presidents.

name: Batad
summary: Batad is a village of Ifugao province in the Cordillera Administrative Region of the island of Luzon in the Philippines.

name: Batan
summary: Batan is a municipality of 32,000 people (2015) in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Batanes
summary: Batanes is the smallest and the northernmost province of the Philippines.

name: Batangas
summary: Batangas (pronounced as “Batang-gas”) is a province in the southern part of Luzon, the main island of the northern Philippines. It is the cradle of the Tagalog culture. Being near to Metro Manila, Batangas is a frequently visited area, with its share of resorts and heritage sites. The province is also a growing destination for pilgrimages with its number of Roman Catholic churches as well as various pilgrimage sites.

name: Batangas City
summary: Batangas (pronounced as “batang-gas”), the capital of Batangas province, is a major seaport, second to Manila among the ports on Luzon, and a gateway to the rest of the archipelago. . Metro Batangas is seeing fast growth, but its prominent sights like the city's religious sites and heritage homes are yet to have a mention to the tourist trail.

name: Bato
summary: Bato is a municipality of the island province of Catanduanes.

name: Bato (Camarines Sur)
summary: Bato is a municipality of Camarines Sur that is home to a lake teeming with various kinds of fishes like tilapia housed in fish cages. Sinarapan, the world's smallest commercially harvested fish, occupies the waters of Lake Bato.

name: Batuan
summary: Batuan is a municipality of Masbate in Ticao island.

name: Bauan
summary: Bauan is a town in Batangas. It is a suburb of Batangas City and is along the route to the resorts of the municipality of Mabini.

name: Bauang
summary: Bauang is a coastal town in La Union. Long dismissed as a stopover on the way to the provincial capital, San Fernando, and the more famous beaches of San Juan, it has its own attractive beaches and heritage monuments of interest.

name: Bayawan
summary: Bayawan is on the southwest coast of Negros Oriental. It is a moderately large town, 118,000 in the 2015 census, and has good beaches but tourism is not highly developed.

name: Baybay
summary: Baybay is a city in the province of Leyte, in the Philippines.

name: Bayombong
summary: Bayombong is the provincial capital of Nueva Vizcaya.

name: Benguet
summary: Benguet is a province in the Cordillera region of Luzon in the Philippines.

name: Bicol
summary: Bicol, also called Bicolandia is a peninsula at the southeastern end of the largest Philippine island of Luzon. It is officially called Bicol Region and designated as Region V. The administrative region comprises six provinces — four provinces on the peninsula and two island provinces. The region is a premier destination for both adventure and culture.

name: Biliran
summary: Biliran is an island province in the Eastern Visayas, between Leyte Island and Samar Island. The province has many smaller islands and islets, beautiful and pristine white sand beaches and waterfalls.

name: Binangonan
summary: Binangonan is a town in the province of Rizal, Philippines. At the boundary between the urban conurbation extending from Metro Manila and the rural towns of eastern Rizal, it has posh hillside resorts, chronically snarled highways, heritage buildings and hiking paradises within its boundaries.

name: Binmaley
summary: Binmaley is a municipality of 89,000 people (2020). Binmaley is the seafood capital of Pangasinan.

name: Bislig
summary: Bislig is in Mindanao.

name: Biñan
summary: Biñan is a city in Laguna. Practically, it is more of a bedroom community south of Manila, but is well recognized as the city where the Philippine national hero, Jose Rizal, received his first education.

name: Boac
summary: Boac is a municipality in the province of Marinduque, in the Philippines and is its capital.

name: Bocaue
summary: Bocaue (pronounced as bo-ka-we) is a town in Bulacan. It is noted for its fireworks industry, its famous fluvial parade, the largest indoor stadium in the world. Bocaue is nicknamed the "Fireworks Capital of the Philippines", with its many local manufacturers and fireworks stores.

name: Bogo
summary: Bogo City is on Cebu Island.

name: Bohol
summary: Bohol is the main island of Bohol Province, which also includes 75 smaller islands. The island lies southeast from Cebu Island and southwest of Leyte Island in the Central Visayas region. This oval-shaped island is the tenth largest of the Philippine archipelago.

name: Bolinao
summary: Bolinao is a rural municipality in Pangasinan. It is approximately 375 km by land from Manila.

name: Bolod and Libaong
summary: Bolod and Libaong are barangays on Panglao Island in the Philippines, east of the island's main tourist area Alona Beach.

name: Bongabon
summary: Bongabon is a municipality in Nueva Ecija. Situated on the slopes of the Sierra Madre, it forms one of the gateways to neigboring Aurora province.

name: Bongao
summary: Bongao is the capital of the province of Tawi-Tawi in the Sulu Islands, part of the Bangsamoro autonomous region.

name: Bontoc
summary: __TOC__ Bontoc is a city in Mountain Province of the Luzon Cordilleras.

name: Boracay
summary: Boracay is a tropical island about an hour's flight from Metro Manila in the Philippines. It has superb long white sand beaches and is one of the country's most developed tourist destinations.

name: Borongan
summary: Borongan is the capital of Eastern Samar, in the Eastern Visayas region of the Philippines. The city is a surfer's paradise, mostly frequented during the cool, rainy months.

name: Boston (Davao Oriental)
summary: Boston is a town in Davao Oriental in the Philippines.

name: Botolan
summary: Botolan is a town of the province of Zambales in the Philippines. Situated at the foot of the Mount Pinatubo massif, it combines cultural heritage and natural wonders within its territory, despite challenges brought by the Mount Pinatubo eruption in 1991.

name: Brooke's Point
summary: Brooke's Point is a 1st class municipality in the province of Palawan, Philippines. According to the 2015 census, it has an estimated population of 66,374. The municipality has become famous for its promotion of ecotourism.

name: Buhi
summary: Buhi is a municipality in Camarines Sur which contains the eponymous lake. The town borders the province of Albay in the south. It is the only town in Rinconada District that does not speak Rinconada but instead speaks the variety of Bikol language called Buhinon

name: Bulacan
summary: Bulacan is a province in the Philippines. It is located just north of Metro Manila and shares boundaries with Pampanga and Nueva Ecija in the north, and Manila Bay on the south west.

name: Bulakan
summary: Bulakan is a town in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. A former provincial capital, it is relatively quieter than its neighboring towns that have become noisy thoroughfares on the Philippine highway network and manages to retain monuments from its colonial and revolutionary past. In the future, it will be the site of the New Manila International Airport in the Taliptip area.

name: Burauen
summary: Burauen is a municipality in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Burgos (Ilocos Norte)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see Burgos (disambiguation).
Burgos is a town in Ilocos Norte, Philippines. Strategically located at the northwesternmost corner of Luzon, it is known for the lighthouse that looms over Cape Bojeador into the South China Sea.

name: Burgos (La Union)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see Burgos (disambiguation).
Burgos is a town in La Union.

name: Burgos (Pangasinan)
summary: Burgos is a municipality of 24,000 people (2020) in the province of Pangasinan. It is home of some natural wonders like white-sand beaches and waterfalls.

name: Buruanga
summary: Buruanga is a municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines, to its north is where Malay, Aklan and to its south is where municipality of Libertad, Antique is located while to its west lies Cuyo Sea. See Buruanga for its beautiful mangroves and beautiful rock formations which make it an "off the beaten path" destination.

name: Buscalan
summary: Buscalan is a mountain village in Kalinga, in the Luzon Cordilleras. It is the home of Butbut tribe, who used to be fierce headhunters.

name: Busuanga Island
summary: Busuanga is the largest Island of the Calamian archipelago in the northern part of Palawan province in the Philippines. Nice beaches, gentle landscape, good hiking and great diving make the island a good holiday destination.

name: Butuan
summary: Butuan is a city in the province of Agusan del Norte in the Philippines. Located in the northeastern part of Agusan Valley sprawling across the Agusan River, the city is known for its colorful history and culture.

name: Cabagan
summary: Cabagan is a municipality of Isabela.

name: Cabanatuan
summary: Cabanatuan is a city in Nueva Ecija in the Philippines. It is the "Gateway to the North", a secondary commercial center of Central Luzon, and the former capital of the Philippines' "Rice Granary".

name: Cabangan
summary: Cabangan (pronounced as “Kabang-gan”) is a town of the province of Zambales in the Philippines.

name: Cabarroguis
summary: Cabarroguis is a the capital of the province of Quirino.

name: Cabugao
summary: Cabugao is a coastal town in Ilocos Sur.

name: Cabuyao
summary: Cabuyao is a city in Laguna, a region in the Philippines. It covers the southern banks of Laguna de Bay, the largest lake in the country, and its rapidly increasing number of inhabitants now lies around 250,000. It is an industrial centre and the regional business seat for many multinationals operating in the Philippines. As such, it holds little interest for travellers.

name: Cagayan
summary: Cagayan is a province in the Cagayan Valley region of Luzon.

name: Cagayan Valley
summary: Cagayan Valley is a region at the northeastern corner of Luzon. The regional center is Tuguegarao, and is composed of five provinces in administrative terms, namely: Batanes, Cagayan, Isabela, Nueva Vizcaya and Quirino. This guide only covers the mainland areas: Batanes is treated as a separate region for its isolation and distinct culture.

name: Cagayan de Oro
summary: Cagayan de Oro, often abbreviated CDO and sometimes just called "Cagayan", is known as the "City of Golden Friendship." It is the capital of the Province of Misamis Oriental and the "Gateway of Northern Mindanao."

name: Cagayancillo
summary: Cagayancillo is a municipality in Palawan Province, a group of 31 islands in the middle of the Sulu Sea. It is a bit closer to Negros Occidental than to Palawan Island. Cagayancillo is the closest settlement to the Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park.

name: Cainta
summary: Cainta (pronounced as “Ka-inta”) is a town in Rizal, Philippines. Now part of Manila's ever-expanding sprawl, Cainta is considered the gateway to the province.

name: Calabanga
summary: Calabanga is a town of 89,000 people (2020) north of Naga City, Camarines Sur.

name: Calabarzon
summary: Calabarzon is a region of southwestern Luzon, the main island in the Philippines.

name: Calaguas Islands
summary: Calaguas is a common reference to a group of islands, northeast of Vinzons, Camarines Norte, Paracale and Daet towns in Camarines Norte in the Philippines. It is composed of three major islands; Tinaga Island, Guintinua Island and Maculabo Island and other small islets. Tinaga Island is the most popular to backpackers from Manila and elsewhere due to its famous white sand beach called Mahabang Buhangin, which literally means 'long beach'. Mahabang Buhangin rivals the fine sands of Boracay, a popular tourist destination in the Philippines.

name: Calamba
summary: Calamba is a city in Laguna, Philippines, a major economic, transportation, and tourist hub in the Calabarzon region. It is the birthplace and ancestral location of the Philippines' National Hero, Jose Rizal, and one barangay, Pansol, is home to various hot spring resorts near Mount Makiling.

name: Calamian Islands
summary: The Calamian Islands or Calamianes are in Palawan province in the Philippines. They are located northeast of Palawan Island, across a straight from Mindoro. The most important town is Coron which is a popular dive resort, partly because a battle during World War II left many sunken ships in the immediate area.

name: Calapan
summary: Calapan is the provincial capital city of Oriental Mindoro, Philippines.

name: Calasiao
summary: Calasiao is a municipality in Pangasinan.

name: Calatagan
summary: Calatagan is a municipality in Batangas.

name: Calbayog
summary: Calbayog is a city of 183,000 in Samar Province in the Philippines. It is home to many waterfalls, so its nickname "City of Waterfalls". Calbayog is a stop along the Asian Highway 26 or the Maharlika Highway.

name: Calbiga
summary: Calbiga is a growing agricultural and educational municipality of Samar Province in the Philippines. It lies along the Pan-Philippine (Maharlika) Highway and is said to be the land of beauty in the Province of Samar.

name: Caloocan
summary: Caloocan or Kalookan is a city in northern Metro Manila. Caloocan is a large suburb of Manila, and is predominantly residential, mostly home to people relocated from Manila's slums. There is also a noticeable lack of tourist attractions.

name: Calumpit
summary: Calumpit is a town in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. It is the gateway to Pampanga.

name: Camalig
summary: Camalig is a landlocked municipality in Albay along the Asian Highway 26. It is the nearest to Mayon Volcano and features a scenic landscapes and countryside. Separates the municipalities of Guinobatan and Daraga, it is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Camarines Norte
summary: Camarines Norte is the northernmost province in Bicol Region of the Philippines. It is a largely rainy and forested region; it is less visited than nearby Camarines Sur, but it has hidden beaches, little-explored mountains and small towns with historic churches. Camarines Norte has a Tagalog-influenced Bicolano culture

name: Camarines Sur
summary: Camarines Sur, often shortened to CamSur, is the largest of the six provinces of Bicol Region and falls between the provinces of Camarines Norte in the north and Albay in the south. It is rich in nature, history, and culture, from the heritage churches of some small towns, to the smallest commercially-bred fish to the pink and black sand beaches of the Partido district.

name: Camiguin
summary: Camiguin is a small island province off the northern coast of Mindanao in the Philippines.

name: Camiling
summary: Camiling is a town located in the province of Tarlac in Central Luzon, the Philippines.

name: Camotes Islands
summary: The Camotes are a small island group in the Philippines. Administratively, they are part of Cebu Province but they are some distance east of Cebu Island (63 km from Cebu City), actually closer to Leyte.

name: Candaba
summary: Candaba is a town in northeastern Pampanga, Philippines. It is named after the swamp that separates it from Bulacan.

name: Candelaria (Quezon)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Candelaria (disambiguation).
Candelaria is a town in western Quezon. Located at the foot of Mount Banahaw, it is a growing commercial agricultural town with a few natural and man-made attractions in between.

name: Candon
summary: Candon is a city in Ilocos Sur province of the Philippines. One of two designated cities in the province, it is overshadowed by the more famous capital, Vigan, but takes pride as the province's economic center and largest city.

name: Canigao Island
summary: Canigao is an islet in the municipality of Matalom, Leyte. The area is known for abundant fishing grounds and scenic coral reef areas suitable for diving.

name: Capas
summary: Capas is a municipality in the southern part of Tarlac. Dubbed the "Tourism Capital of Tarlac", Capas is known as the endpoint of the infamous Death March during World War II, and is the jumping point for treks to Mount Pinatubo, which have its devastating eruption in 1991.

name: Capiz
summary: Capiz is a province on the island of Panay in the Western Visayas.

name: Capul
summary:
Capul is a municipality in Northern Samar, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.
In 2020 census, it has a population of 12,000.

name: Caraga
summary: Caraga is a region in the northeastern corner of Mindanao in the Philippines.

name: Caramoan
summary: Caramoan is a municipality of the Philippines in the province of Camarines Sur in the island of Luzon.

name: Carcar
summary: Carcar is an old colonial town on the coast south of Cebu City.

name: Cardona (Rizal)
summary: Cardona is a town in the province of Rizal, Philippines. At the boundary between the urban conurbation extending from Metro Manila and eastern Rizal, it is a fishing and agriculture-oriented town where rural Rizal is said to begin.

name: Carigara
summary: Carigara is a municipality of 55,000 people (2020) in the northern part of Leyte province on the shores of Carigara Bay. It is surrounded by wide rice fields fanning out towards the mountains in the distance.

name: Carmen (Bohol)
summary: Carmen is the most common area to stay overnight if you would like to visit the Chocolate Hills in Bohol.

name: Carranglan
summary: Carranglan is a municipality in Nueva Ecija. It is a highland town in the middle of the Caraballo Mountains that is dubbed the “Gateway to Cagayan Valley” and the “Little Baguio” and “Summer Capital” of Nueva Ecija for its cool climate.

name: Catanduanes
summary: Catanduanes is an island province of the Philippines, located in the Bicol Region, off the eastern coast of the Bicol Peninsula.

name: Catarman
summary: Catarman is the capital of Northern Samar, in the Eastern Visayas, Philippines. It is on the northern coast of Samar Island. It is the commercial, educational, financial, political and government center of the province.

name: Catbalogan
summary: Catbalogan is the capital city of Samar Province, in Eastern Visayas, Philippines. It is also the commercial, trading, educational, political and financial centre of Samar. It lies along the Pan-Philippine (Maharlika) Highway and is the gateway to the region's three Samar provinces. It has been long known as the "Gateway to Samar Region."

name: Cauayan (Isabela)
summary: Cauayan is a city in Isabela. It is the center of the tobacco industry in Cagayan Valley, and is also an important economic hub, mostly concentrated on agriculture, services and industry.

name: Cauayan (Negros Occidental)
summary: Cauayan is a municipality in Negros Oriental with a population of a little over 100,000. There is a lot of coast with good fishing and some fine beaches, but inland parts of the municipality are mountainous. The area's main attraction is Danjugan Island; the island itself is a wildlife sanctuary and the surrounding waters are a marine sanctuary with excellent diving.

name: Cavinti
summary: Cavinti is a highland town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. It is known for its natural attractions and camp sites, earning it the title of "Glamping Capital of the Philippines".

name: Cavite
summary: Cavite (Tagalog: Kabite) is a province in the Calabarzon region of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. It is the most densely populated province in the Philippines. . Being near to Metro Manila, its northern areas has become characterized by sprawling residential communities, which are continuing to grow until this day, while its southern highlands become a summer getaway for weekenders.

name: Cavite City
summary: Cavite City is a city in Cavite province in the Philippines.

name: Cebu City
summary: Cebu City is the main city on Cebu Island in the Philippines and is known as the Queen City of the South. It is the capital of Cebu Province, a transport hub, and a popular tourist destination in its own right.

name: Cebu Province
summary: Cebu Island is a large island in the Visayas region of the Philippines. Cebu Province is that island plus several nearby small islands. The larger Negros Island lies just across the Tañon Strait to the west. Leyte and Bohol are to the east.

name: Central Luzon
summary: Central Luzon is one of the 18 regions of the Philippines.

name: Central Visayas
summary: The Central Visayas (Region VII) is one of the administrative regions of the Philippines, part of the Visayas island group. The Visayas are roughly the central third of the Philippines, so this region is approximately in the center of the whole country.

name: Cervantes (Ilocos Sur)
summary: Cervantes is a municipality in Ilocos Sur. Situated within the Cordillera mountains, it is dubbed the province's summer capital.

name: Clark (Central Luzon)
summary: Clark is a geographical region in Central Luzon, Philippines.

name: Claveria
summary: Claveria is a coastal municipality in Cagayan on Luzon, the Philippines. It is the primary beach destination in northwestern Cagayan, with an extensive series of beaches and rock formations set amidst background of the Cordillera mountains.

name: Compostela (Cebu)
summary: Compostela is a municipality in Metro Cebu, on the coast north of Cebu City.

name: Concepcion (Tarlac)
summary:
For Concepcion of Chile, see Concepcion. For other cities by the name, see Concepcion (disambiguation).
Concepcion is a town in southern Tarlac. A primarily agricultural town, it is known for being the home of the Aquino political family, which has produced two Philippine presidents.

name: Consolacion (Cebu)
summary: Consolacion is in the Philippines; it is part of Metro Cebu and located just north of Mandaue. .

name: Corella
summary: Corella is a municipality in the province of Bohol just adjacent to the capital city of Tagbilaran.

name: Coron
summary: Coron is a town in the province of Palawan on Busuanga Island. The area is famous for its World War II wreck diving, and the site has been named in many lists of top dive spots in the world. There are many beautiful white sand beaches, mostly tiny and surrounded by large limestone cliffs and wildlife.

name: Corregidor Island
summary: Corregidor Island is a small island in the Philippines. It is well-known for its strategic situation at the opening of Manila Bay.

name: Cotabato City
summary: Cotabato City is the regional center of Bangsamoro region. Cotabato City is the city of cultural charms, because the city is the melting pot of different beliefs like Christians, Muslims and Lumads.

name: Cuenca (Batangas)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Cuenca.
Cuenca is a town in Batangas, on the southern coast of Taal Lake. The town's main tourist draw is Mount Maculot; it is fairly easily climbed and the summit gives a fine view of the lake and volcano. Near the town are a growing number of private resorts, mostly mid-range to splurge.

name: Culion Island
summary: Culion Island is one of the Calamian Islands in Palawan Province of the Philippines. The main town is also called Culion. The municipality includes about 40 smaller islands.

name: Cuyo Islands
summary: The Cuyo Islands are a group of islands in Palawan Province, Philippines. The archipelago is in the Sulu Sea, to the northeast of the main island of Palawan, south of Mindoro and west of Panay. There are 45 islands, many of which are uninhabited. Their total land area is 130 km² (50 square miles); population in 2010 was about 46,000.

name: Córdova (Cebu)
summary: Córdova is a small municipality of around 60,000 in Cebu Province, part of Metro Cebu.

name: Daanbantayan
summary: Daanbantayan is near the northern tip of Cebu Island in the Philippines.

name: Daet
summary: Daet is the provincial capital of Camarines Norte. It is a small town, with a beach popular with surfers.

name: Dagupan
summary: Dagupan is the largest city in Pangasinan. That is not saying it couldn't use a bit of a facelift though. The city is among the top producers of milkfish (locally known as bangus) in the province; it is sometimes called the Bangus Capital City.

name: Danao
summary: Danao is a town on Cebu island, the northernmost town administered as part of Metro Cebu.

name: Danao Beach
summary: Danao Beach is on Panglao Island in the Bohol province of the Philippines.

name: Dapitan
summary: Dapitan, also known as the Shrine City of the Philippines, is a city in the province of Zamboanga del Norte, located on the island of Mindanao, which is the second largest island in the Philippines.

name: Daraga
summary: Daraga is a landlocked municipality in the province of Albay and is flanked by Legazpi, the capital city and the municipality of Camalig. It hosts the Bicol International Airport and is known for the Cagsawa Ruins. This town is located along the Asian Highway 26 and is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Dasmariñas
summary: Dasmariñas, or Dasma in short, is a large city in Cavite. It is at the center or the province, and at the crossroads of two major highways.

name: Dasol
summary: Dasol is a municipality of 29,000 people (2015) in Pangasinan that is inextricably connected to the sea. It has a sizable number of tourism amenities along the beach and other attractions to draw tourism.

name: Dauin
summary: Dauin is a small (about 25,000) seaside municipality south of Dumaguete in Negros Oriental. It is bordered on the east by the seashore, on the north by Bacong, on the south by Zamboanguita, and on the west by Santa Catalina.

name: Dauis
summary: Dauis is on Panglao Island in Bohol, Phlippines.

name: Davao
summary: Davao is the largest city on the Philippines' second-largest island, Mindanao. It has a huge land area, and the inhabitants like to think of it as one of the most crime-free large cities in the Philippines.

name: Davao Oriental
summary: Davao Oriental is a province in Davao Region. It is the easternmost province of the Philippines and is dubbed as “Sunrise Capital” as it is the first to greet the dawn each day. The province offers a captivating blend of natural beauty and rich local traditions.

name: Davao Region
summary: Davao Region is on the island of Mindanao, Philippines. It used to be one province, but it has since been divided into five.

name: Diffun
summary: Diffun (pronounced "dif-foon") is a municipality in Quirino. It is the most populated town in the province and its main port of entry.

name: Digos
summary: Digos is the provincial capital of Davao Del Sur. It is nicknamed as the "Mango Capital of the Philippines".

name: Dinapigue
summary: Dinapigue is a municipality on the Pacific coast of Isabela province in the northern part of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. Cut off from the rest of the country by the Sierra Madre mountains, it is one of the least explored areas of the province, but is being geared as its future beach tourism destination.

name: Dingalan
summary: Dingalan (pronounced as ding-galan) is a municipality on the Pacific coast of Aurora province in the central part of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. Cut off from the rest of the country by the Sierra Madre mountains, it is one of the least explored areas of the province, but is being dubbed as the "Batanes of the East" due to similarities in their natural setting.

name: Dipolog
summary: Dipolog is the capital city of the province of Zamboanga del Norte, the province that occupies the northern part of Zamboanga Peninsula in the Mindanao island of the Philippines. It is commonly known as the "Bottled Sardines Capital" due to its sardine production, and most popularly the "Gateway to Western Mindanao" being accessible from Dumaguete, Cebu, and Manila.

name: Diving in the Philippines
summary: This article is intended to provide the already qualified Scuba diver with information which will help to plan dives in the waters of the Philippines, whether as a local resident or a visitor. Information is provided without prejudice, and is not guaranteed accurate or complete. Use it at your own risk.

name: Dolores (Quezon)
summary: Dolores is a town in western Quezon. Situated at the foot of the Mount Banahaw range, it is a primarily agricultural town that is also a pilgrimage site for animists and syncretics who believe in Banahaw's spiritual prowess.

name: Donsol
summary: Donsol is a municipality in the province of Sorsogon, Philippines. It's known for the eco-tourism activity involving an interaction with the whale sharks.

name: Doña Remedios Trinidad
summary: Doña Remedios Trinidad (commonly abbreviated to DRT) is a municipality in the province of Bulacan in the Philippines. One of the geographically largest yet least populated towns in the country, it is home to less known natural attractions along the Sierra Madre mountains.

name: Dumaguete
summary: Dumaguete is the capital city and main port of Negros Oriental, the province that occupies the south-eastern part of Negros Island, in the Philippines. It is sometimes called the "City of Gentle People".

name: Dupax
summary: Dupax is a historic town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Having been split into northern and southern halves since 1978, it counts natural and Spanish-era monuments among its attractions.

name: Eastern Laguna
summary: The eastern portion of Laguna is a rough agglomeration of 16 towns sandwiched between the eastern shores of Laguna de Bay and the western slopes of the Sierra Madre mountains and Mount Banahaw. It is where the rural and wild portion of the province can be seen unhindered by the urbanization to its west.

name: Eastern Samar
summary: Eastern Samar is a province forming the eastern part of Samar Island in the Philippines.

name: Eastern Visayas
summary: Eastern Visayas is one of the four administrative regions in the Visayas group of islands, and is designated Region VIII out of the 17 regions of the entire Philippines.

name: El Nido
summary: El Nido is a coastal town in Palawan. El Nido comprises 45 islands and islets; limestone cliffs are also found here, which form a Karst backdrop similar to those found in Ha Long Bay, Krabi and Guilin. It is a popular destination for locals during the long holidays of the Holy Week, but has been relatively unknown to foreign tourists. El Nido is more than just a stereotypical tropical paradise. Beaches, clear waters, jungle, steep limestone cliffs and stunning inlets make for one of the world's most beautiful seascapes.

name: Floridablanca
summary: Floridablanca is a town in southwestern Pampanga. Situated at the boundary of the Central Luzon plains and the Zambales mountain range, it combines a military airfield, cultural heritage and natural wonders within its territory.

name: Gamu
summary: Gamu is a town of Isabela. A suburb of the provincial capital Ilagan, it is the pilgrimage center of Isabela, hosting a cathedral, a Marian shrine, and a monastery.

name: Gapan
summary: Gapan is a city in Nueva Ecija. Although overshadowed by Cabanatuan to the north, it retains a number of significant heritage sites while retaining its status as the economic center of southern Nueva Ecija.

name: Gasan
summary: Gasan is a town in the province of Marinduque in the Philippines. With 33,000 people living within town limits, it is the province's third-largest town in terms of population, and is often called the cultural capital of Marinduque.

name: General Santos
summary: General Santos or "GenSan" is a city in the province of South Cotabato in Soccsksargen. It is known as "The Tuna Capital of the Philippines" due to its tuna industry. Perhaps its biggest claim to fame is that boxer Manny Pacquiao is a native.

name: General Trias
summary: General Trias (commonly shortened into GenTri) is a city in Cavite. Though now part of the immense urban sprawl of northern Cavite from the 1980s, it still contains some sights of historic importance.

name: Getafe (Bohol)
summary: Getafe or Jetafe is a seaside town of 33,000 people (2019) at the northwest corner of Bohol.

name: Gingoog
summary: Gingoog is a city in Northern Mindanao. Gingoog is known as the vacation city of Misamis Oriental, not only because of the beautiful places to visit but because of the beautiful and hospitable people who reside therein.

name: Goa (Camarines Sur)
summary: Goa is a municipality in Partido area of Camarines Sur. It is the educational center of Partido area as it hosts the Partido State University.

name: Gonzaga
summary: Gonzaga is a coastal municipality in Cagayan on Luzon, the Philippines. It is home to the only active volcano in northern Luzon and extensive beaches.

name: Guagua
summary: Guagua is a town in southwestern Pampanga. A municipality created from the merger of four settlements, it is best known for the woodcarving traditions and intricately painted interior of the colonial-era parish church of Betis district, although the rest of Guagua has touristic assets of its own such as Guagua's parish church, which also dates from the colonial era, and a significant number of heritage structures and residences that survived the ravages of World War II and the eruption of Mount Pinatubo in 1991.

name: Guihulngan
summary: Guihulngan is a coastal town in the north of Negros Oriental. It is the province's third largest city with 103,000 residents in 2020.

name: Guimaras
summary: Guimaras is a small island province in the Western Visayas region of the Philippines. It is in the strait between two larger islands, Panay and Negros.

name: Guinobatan
summary: Guinobatan is a landlocked municipality in the province of Albay, placed between the city of Ligao and the municipality of Camalig accessible via Asian Highway 26. It is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Guiuan
summary: Guiuan is a municipality in Eastern Samar, Philippines. It was the first place in the Philippines where Europeans landed; Magellan's expedition reached here in March 1521.

name: Gumaca
summary: Gumaca is a town along the Pacific coast of Quezon province, Philippines.

name: Hagonoy
summary: Hagonoy is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. It is a vibrant fishing community with natural and heritage attractions along the Angat-Pampanga River delta that carries on despite being endangered by rising sea levels from Manila Bay.

name: Hilongos
summary: Hilongos is a municipality in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Hingyon
summary: Hingyon is a town in Ifugao, a province in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. Often dismissed as a stopover on the way to Banaue, it offers some of the typical attractions of the province but with lesser tourists to share space with.

name: Hungduan
summary: Hungduan is a town in Ifugao, a province in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. It has some of the famous Rice Terraces of the Cordilleras inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List.

name: Iba
summary: Iba is the capital of the province of Zambales in the Philippines.

name: Ibajay
summary: Ibajay is a municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines. It has a population of about 40,000.

name: Ifugao
summary: Ifugao is a province in the Cordillera region of Luzon in the Philippines. It is known for its rice terraces, some of which have been designated as World Heritage Sites by UNESCO.

name: Iguig
summary: Iguig (pronounced “Ee-geeg”) is a town of Cagayan. A suburb of the provincial capital Tuguegarao, it is is known for its multiple pilgrimage spots.

name: Ilagan
summary: Ilagan is the capital city of Isabela. It is one of the largest cities in the Philippines, but it has a small town feel, and has a vibrant tourism scene. It is along the main highway to Tuguegarao.

name: Iligan
summary: Iligan is a city in the northeastern coast of Northern Mindanao, surrounded by the towns of Baloi and Linamon of Lanao del Norte to the south, the town of Lugait in Misamis Oriental to the north, and the provinces of Lanao del Sur and Bukidnon to the east and Iligan Bay to the west.

name: Ilocos
summary: Ilocos, officially named Ilocos Region and administratively designated Region I, forms the northwest part of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. It is known for its old towns, historical sites, beaches, and nature attractions.

name: Ilocos Norte
summary: Ilocos Norte is a province in the Ilocos Region, north of the Philippines.

name: Ilocos Sur
summary: Ilocos Sur is a province in the Ilocos Region of the Philippines.

name: Iloilo (province)
summary: Iloilo is a province on the island of Panay in the Philippines.

name: Iloilo City
summary: Iloilo City is the provincial capital of Iloilo, on the island of Panay. The city is rich in history and culture, with well-preserved Spanish and American-era architecture, from churches to commercial buildings and the many ancestral houses scattered around the city. It’s also known for its distinct and flavorful cuisine, earning the recognition of being named a UNESCO City of Gastronomy.

name: Imus
summary: Imus is a city in Cavite, and the de jure capital of the province. The city is the site of Battle of Alapan, a major encounter during the Philippine Revolution on 1898. Though now part of the immense sprawl of northern Cavite from the 1980s, it still contains some sights of historic importance.

name: Indang
summary: Indang is a municipality, an inland tourist destination at the southern part of Cavite. The town center houses the Spanish-era church, the public market, and the main campus of Cavite State University; the resorts are scattered around the 32 barangays.

name: Infanta
summary: Infanta is a city of 26,000 people (2020) in Pangasinan province in northern Luzon.

name: Inopacan
summary: Inopacan is a city of about 21,000 people (2015) in the western part of Leyte, in Leyte province.

name: Ipil
summary: Ipil is the capital of the province of Zamboanga Sibugay on the Zamboanga Peninsula.

name: Iriga
summary: Iriga is a city in Camarines Sur, at the center of the Rinconada District where residents speak Rinconada, a unique variety of Bikol language.

name: Isabela (city)
summary: Isabela is a city in Basilan, an island on the Sulu Archipelago in southern Philippines.

name: Isabela (province)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Isabela.
Isabela is the second largest province in the Philippines in land area. It is in the Cagayan Valley.

name: Isulan
summary: Isulan is a town of almost 100,000 people (2022). It is also the capital of the province of Sultan Kudarat.

name: Itbayat
summary: Itbayat is an island municipality of Batanes province in the northern Philippines.

name: Itogon
summary: Itogon is a municipality in the province of Benguet, Philippines.

name: Ivana
summary: Ivana is a municipality of Batanes province in the northern Philippines.

name: Jagna
summary: Jagna is a small port town of 34,000 people (2015) on the south coast of Bohol. It is to the east of Tagbilaran, which is the provincial capital and has the main seaport and only airport of the province.

name: Jalajala
summary: Jalajala, sometimes spelled as Jala-Jala and pronounced as “hala-hala”, is a town in southeastern Rizal, Philippines. Situated at the tip of its eponymous peninsula, it is one of the last remaining bastions of rural life in the province.

name: Jolo
summary: Jolo is a volcanic island in the southwest Philippines and is the primary island of the province of Sulu in Bangsamoro. The main city of the island, also called Jolo, is the capital of the province.

name: Jovellar
summary: Jovellar is a landlocked municipality in the southwest quadrant of Albay in the Philippines and borders Donsol in the province of Sorsogon.

name: Kabankalan
summary: Kabankalan is a city in the province of Negros Occidental, Philippines.

name: Kabayan
summary: Kabayan is a municipality in the province of Benguet, Philippines.

name: Kalayaan (Laguna)
summary: Kalayaan is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines.

name: Kalibo
summary: Kalibo is the capital of the province of Aklan, Philippines. It is a large town, with an airport that serves as the main gateway for Boracay, and a rich culture.

name: Kalinga
summary: Kalinga (pronounced as “Kaling-ga”) is a province in the Cordillera region of Luzon in the Philippines. Long feared for its tribal conflicts and headhunters, it is nowadays renowned for its natural and cultural attractions such as indigenous villages, whitewater rafting, unspoiled mountains and even an indigenous tattoo artist.

name: Kasibu
summary: Kasibu is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. It is the province's "citrus capital" due to its extensive production of the fruit, and also has multiple natural attractions and indigenous tribes coexisting uneasily with one of the largest gold mining operations in the country.

name: Kawit
summary: Kawit is a municipality in Cavite. It is famous for being the place where Philippine independence was proclaimed in 1898 and for being the hometown of the Philippines' first president, Emilio Aguinaldo.

name: Kayapa
summary: Kayapa is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated within the Cordillera Mountains, it is the main point of entry leading to the Cagayan Valley region from Baguio and is dubbed the “Summer Capital” of Nueva Vizcaya for its highland location and cool climate.

name: Kiangan
summary: Kiangan is a town in Ifugao, a province in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. One of the province's cultural capitals, it is famous for its rice terraces and for being the site of Japanese general Tomoyuki Yamashita's surrender at the end of World War II.

name: Kidapawan
summary: Kidapawan is the capital city of Cotabato Province with a rapidly growing population of more than 161,000 (2020).

name: Koronadal
summary: Koronadal is a city in South Cotabato, Soccsksargen, Philippines.

name: La Trinidad (Benguet)
summary: La Trinidad is a small town which serves as the capital of the province of Benguet which is part of the Cordillera Administrative Region of the Philippines. Tourists to the town mostly come from the neighboring city of Baguio.

name: La Union
summary: La Union, also known as L.U. in short, is a province in the Ilocos region of the Philippines.

name: Labo
summary: Labo is a municipality in Camarines Norte, Philippines, known for its rich agricultural heritage, scenic mountains, waterfalls, and the Busig-on River. Its culture and natural resources are celebrated through local festivals, particularly the Busig-on Festival, reflecting the creativity, traditions, and warm hospitality of the Laboeños.

name: Laguna
summary: Laguna is a province in the Calabarzon region of the island of Luzon in the Philippines, wrapped around the large lake Laguna de Bay. It is one of the most progressive, historical and cultural provinces in the Philippines.

name: Laguna Caldera District
summary: The Laguna Caldera District of Rizal is a rough agglomeration of seven towns along the Morong and Jalajala peninsulas that comprise the remnants of the Laguna Caldera, an inactive underwater volcano that forms the central lobe of Laguna de Bay, the largest lake in the Philippines.

name: Lake Sebu
summary: Lake Sebu is a town in South Cotabato and is the name of the eponymous lake.

name: Lal-lo
summary: Lal-lo, Gattaran (pronounced as “Gat-taran”) and Lasam are three rural municipalities in northern Cagayan. The former have the Lal-lo and Gattaran Shell Middens and the Magapit Protected Landscape, while Lasam is a smaller municipality that used to be part of Gattaran until 1950.

name: Lanao del Sur
summary: Lanao del Sur is a province in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM), Mindanao, Philippines.

name: Laoag
summary: Laoag is the capital city of Ilocos Norte. It is the province's political, commercial, and industrial hub. The historic scenic tourist spots makes Laoag an ecotourism center. For geographical reasons, this guide includes the neighboring towns of Sarrat and San Nicolas.

name: Laoang
summary: Laoang is a municipality in Northern Samar, Eastern Visayas, Philippines. Laoang serves as the economic center of the Northeastern Pacific region. In 2022, it had a population of 62,000.

name: Lapu-Lapu
summary: Lapu-Lapu is an island city of Cebu Province in the Philippines, part of Metro Cebu. .

name: Las Piñas
summary: Las Piñas is a suburban city in southern Metro Manila.

name: Legazpi
summary: Legazpi is the capital city of Albay and the regional center of Bicol Region. It is one of the three cities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano. The city is bounded on the west by the municipality of Daraga and by the municipality of Santo Domingo on the northeast. Its coastline is on the Albay Gulf with whale shark sightings. With the nicknames of "Queen City of South Luzon" and "City of Fun and Adventure", it is a city full of adventure and history.

name: Lemery
summary: Lemery is a major municipality in Batangas. It is a commercial center for the eastern portion of western Batangas. The town lies next to and to the west of the heritage town of Taal; together they form a single urban area. The boundary runs along the Pansipit River; the river area was part of the sea until it was buried by tephra deposits from the 1755 eruption of Taal Volcano.

name: Leyte Island
summary: Leyte is an island in the Eastern Visayas island group in the Philippines. It is divided into two provinces, Leyte Province and Southern Leyte. Each province includes some nearby smaller islands. Leyte is connected by bridges across narrow straits to the larger Samar Island and to the smaller Biliran island. The two largest cities are the capital, Tacloban, on the east coast near Samar Island, and Ormoc on the western coast.

name: Lian
summary: Lian is a municipality in Batangas, just south of Nasugbu.

name: Libacao
summary: Libacao is a municipality of 28,000 people (2020) in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Libmanan
summary: Libmanan is a municipality in northwestern part of Camarines Sur.

name: Libon
summary: Libon is a coastal municipality in the northwest quadrant of Albay. Along with neighboring Polangui, it borders the municipality of Bato, a town in Rinconada District of Camarines Sur. Its coastline faces Burias Pass and is home to Pantao Port, which links Bicol to Masbate, Visayas and Mindanao.

name: Ligao
summary: Ligao is a city in the west coast of Albay in the Philippines. It is a young city, having only given that status in 2001, and is largely agricultural in background. Located along Asian Highway 26, Ligao's shoreline faces Burias Pass. Lies between the municipality of Oas on the north and the municipality of Guinobatan on the south, this city is one of the three cities that has jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Liliw
summary: Liliw is a town in Laguna, in the Philippines. Liliw is one of the oldest towns in Laguna, having existed as a settlement before the Spanish conquest. This town, nestled at the foot of Mount Banahaw, has multiple cold springs, a sizeable number of heritage houses and has a vibrant shoemaking industry that rivals the one in Marikina.

name: Liloan (Metro Cebu)
summary: Liloan or Lilo-an is in Cebu Province, Philippines, a suburb located on the coast north of Cebu City.

name: Limasawa
summary: Limasawa is an island municipality in Southern Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Linapacan
summary: Linapacan is an island in the Calamian Islands group at the north end of Palawan Province. There is also a town named Linapacan.

name: Lingayen
summary: Lingayen (pronounced as “Ling-ga-yen”) is a town, the provincial capital of Pangasinan, known for its long and wide beach.

name: Lipa
summary: Lipa is the second largest city in Batangas, in terms of land area and the economic and religious center of the province. It lies approximately in the middle of the province, surrounded by Malvar to the north, San Pablo and Alaminos (in Laguna), and San Antonio (in Quezon) to the east, Padre Garcia, San Jose and Ibaan to the south, and Cuenca, Mataasnakahoy, and Taal Lake to the west.

name: Loboc
summary: Loboc is a municipality in Bohol Island, Philippines. It is known for its tarsier sanctuary and river cruise.

name: Los Baños
summary: Los Baños is a resort and university town in Laguna, located south of Metro Manila across the country's largest lake, Laguna de Bay. Commonly called LB or Elbi, it is 63 km from Manila and is a popular weekend destination for residents. It is largely a satellite community of adjacent Calamba.

name: Lubang
summary: The Lubang Island Group is in the Philippines, administered as part of Occidental Mindoro province but geographically a separate group of islands northwest of Mindoro. There are seven islands in the group; Lubang Island is the largest at 125 km2 (48 mi2). Population in the 2015 census was just under 29,000.

name: Lubao
summary: Lubao is a town in southwestern Pampanga. It is the gateway to Bataan and Zambales provinces.

name: Lucban
summary: Lucban is a town in Quezon, on the foot of Mount Banahaw.

name: Lucena
summary: Lucena is a city in Quezon Province, and the provincial capital.

name: Luisiana
summary: Luisiana is a highland town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. It is known for its cool weather, natural attractions and camp sites, earning it the title of "Little Baguio of Laguna".

name: Lumban
summary: Lumban is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. One of the oldest known settlements in Laguna, it is known for being a center for hand embroidery and Caliraya Lake, an extensive man-made reservoir.

name: Luna
summary:
For the municipality in Apayao, see Luna (Apayao).
Luna is a town in La Union. It has extensive beaches, a Spanish-era watchtower and a Roman Catholic pilgrimage site.

name: Luna (Apayao)
summary:
For the municipality in La Union, see Luna.
Luna is a town in Apayao. It is the province's economic hub, de facto administrative capital and primary port of entry.

name: Luzon
summary: Luzon is the largest and the most populous island of the Philippines. This article also covers a number of nearby smaller islands.

name: Luzon Cordilleras
summary: The Cordilleras is a highland region in the northern part of Luzon. Its landscape and geography is dominated by the Cordillera Central, which also extends to parts of nearby Ilocos Region to the west and south, and Cagayan Valley to the east and north. This article only covers the area forming the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR).

name: Maasin
summary: Maasin is a city and the capital of Southern Leyte. It is located at the southern tip of Leyte island.

name: Mabinay
summary: Mabinay (stress on middle syllable) is a municipality covering a large area of hills and valleys near the center of Negros Island. There are many caves in the region and the town's small tourist industry revolves around organizing trips to them and kayaking in the Ilog river and its tributaries.

name: Mabini
summary: Mabini is a municipality in Batangas lying on a peninsula overlooking Batangas and Balayan Bays, and considered the birthplace of Philippine's scuba diving industry. Its beach resorts are not far from Manila. Though largely a destination for middle-class locals, it also gets quite a few foreigner visitors, especially divers.

name: Mabini (Pangasinan)
summary: Mabini is a municipality in the province of Pangasinan.

name: Mabitac
summary: Mabitac is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. It is an alternate gateway to the province from Rizal for those seeking to avoid the chronic traffic congestion in the rest of Laguna.

name: Macabebe
summary: Macabebe is a municipality in the province of Pampanga, Philippines. It is a primarily commercial and fishing town at the edge of the Pampanga River delta. The guide also covers the municipality of Masantol, which is almost surrounded by Macabebe and is mainly accessible through it.

name: Maddela
summary: Maddela (pronounced "mad-dela") is a municipality in Quirino.

name: Magalang
summary: Magalang is a town in northern Pampanga, Philippines. Situated at the foot of Mount Arayat and the border with Tarlac province, it combines cultural heritage, agrarian settings and natural wonders within its territory, despite encroaching urbanization from nearby Angeles.

name: Magalawa Island
summary: Magalawa is one of the 19 barangays in the municipality of Palauig, Province of Zambales, Philippines.

name: Magallanes (Sorsogon)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Magallanes (disambiguation).
Magallanes is a municipality of the province of Sorsogon.

name: Magdalena (Laguna)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Magdalena.
Magdalena is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. Situated at the transition zone between the province's lakeside lowlands and the foothills of the Sierra Made and Mount Banahaw, it is dubbed as the "Little Hollywood of Laguna" due to it being a favorite shooting location for domestic television shows and films.

name: Magsingal
summary: Magsingal (pronounced as “Magsing-gal”) is a coastal town in Ilocos Sur.

name: Majayjay
summary: Majayjay (pronounced as “mah-high-HIGH”) is a highland town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. Situated at the northern slopes of Mount Banahaw, it is known for its waterfalls, Spanish-era bridges and Romanesque Catholic basilica.

name: Makati
summary: Makati lies in the heart of Metro Manila. The city is known for its upscale shopping malls with high fashion brands, restaurants and hotels, and is home to many affluent Filipinos. Makati is considered to be a financial, commercial and economic center; it is home to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE).

name: Malabon
summary: Malabon City is a city in Metro Manila, known for its wide variety of seafoods and the well-known noodle, the pancit malabon.

name: Malapascua
summary: Malapascua is an island in Cebu Province north of Cebu Island. The first image Malapascua offers will stay with you for a long time: an exceedingly beautiful pristine stretch of white sand, crystal clear waters bordered by coconut trees and a dozen scattered native-style resorts. But as with all up-and-coming islands experiencing a boom in tourism, Malapascua is rapidly becoming a second Boracay with modern concrete hotels to cater for the varied needs of the many. Despite this modernization, even the largest of resorts embrace the native build styles for a portion of their rooms. The north of the island remains untouched where the fishermen are just fishermen in native style houses.

name: Malasiqui
summary: Malasiqui is a municipality in Pangasinan.

name: Malay (Aklan)
summary: Malay is a municipality in Aklan; its main barangay is Caticlan. Most travellers come here en route to Boracay; the commonest route to get there is via Caticlan's port.

name: Malaybalay
summary: Malaybalay City is the provincial capital of Bukidnon Province, on Mindanao Island in the Philippines.

name: Malilipot
summary: Malilipot is a municipality in the east coast of Albay. It is sandwiched between the city of Tabaco and the municipality of Bacacay. Its shoreline faces Lagonoy Gulf. The town is stretching along Legazpi-Tiwi coastal road and is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Malinao
summary: Malinao is a laidback municipality in the northeast quadrant of Albay and sandwiched between the city of Tabaco and the municipality of Tiwi located along the Legazpi-Tiwi Coastal Road. Its shoreline is facing Lagonoy Gulf.

name: Malolos
summary: Malolos is a city in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. It is the capital of Bulacan and occupies a special place in Philippine history as the capital of an independent Philippines in between the Spanish and American occupations.

name: Malvar
summary: Malvar is a town in Batangas.

name: Manaoag
summary: Manaoag is a town in Pangasinan. It is a popular pilgrimage site for Roman Catholics seeking the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Manaoag.

name: Mandaluyong
summary: Mandaluyong is a city in Metro Manila, Philippines. While not touristy as its neighbors owing to the lack of historical sites, the city is by the way a shopping destination, bordered by Makati to the south, Manila's southeast suburban districts to the west, Pasig to the east, and San Juan and Quezon City to the north.

name: Mandaue
summary: Mandaue is a city in the Philippines, part of Metro Cebu. Mandaue is just north of Cebu City and, like that city, it is on Cebu Island. Just off the coast opposite Mandaue is Mactan Island with the city of Lapu-Lapu on it. From Mandaue two bridges lead to Lapu-Lapu and several good (if sometimes jammed) roads go to Cebu.

name: Mangatarem
summary: Mangatarem is in Pangasinan, Philippines.

name: Manila
summary: Manila (Tagalog: Maynila) is the capital of the Philippines and a major attraction in terms of culture and heritage in the country. Sprawling, congested and polluted will likely be the first words to enter your mind when you think of Manila but don't let that impression stop you from exploring its places of interests: its churches; its diverse and complicated culture; colonial history; gigantic malls; bustling markets; hidden architectural gems and vibrant nightlife. Take the opportunity to explore Manila and make your own personal connection with the city.

name: Manila/Binondo
summary: Binondo is the "Chinatown" district of Manila. It is the oldest Chinatown in the world and was the country's center of commerce during the American occupation. Many of Binondo's commercial establishments were destroyed after World War II, with companies moving to Makati, the financial capital of the Philippines.

name: Manila/Ermita
summary: Ermita is a district in downtown Manila, the capital city of the Philippines.

name: Manila/Intramuros
summary: Intramuros (Latin: within the walls), also known as the Ciudad Murada ("Walled City" in Spanish) because of its most famous feature: a nearly 5-km-long circuit of massive stone walls and fortifications that almost completely surrounds the entire district, is the historic centre and oldest district of Manila, the capital city of the Philippines.

name: Manila/Malate
summary: Malate is an interesting but gritty and dirty area in Manila.

name: Manila/Quiapo
summary: Quiapo is a district in the bustling, busy and crowded city of Manila. Quiapo gets its name from a floating plant named; "Kiapo" that grew abundantly around that area.

name: Manila/Santa Cruz
summary: Santa Cruz is a district in the northern part of the City of Manila on the right bank of the Pasig River near its mouth, bordered by the districts of Tondo, Binondo, Quiapo, and Sampaloc, and Grace Park (Caloocan City) and La Loma (Quezon City).

name: Manila/Southeast
summary: The districts of Paco, Pandacan, San Andres Bukid, and Santa Ana form a vast working-class area on the southeast of Manila. Though they have become homes for the lower class, the districts maintain their history and culture. Paco houses some pieces of historical heritage, like the Paco Park, Paco Train Station, and Plaza Dilao. Santa Ana contains numerous architectural heritage and some archaeological finds, and the only district saved from World War II bombings. Pandacan is rather a district for the lowest classes, and some homeless people living beside the railway tracks, but is noted as the home of some historical figures like Apolinario Mabini and Francisco Baltazar. San Andres Bukid, once rice paddy, is now a large residential area for poorer residents, also jostling for position with

name: Manila/Tondo and San Nicolas
summary: Tondo is a large, culturally diverse district of Manila. Being near to Binondo, many Filipino-Chinese roam around this area, and also have different kinds of businesses situated in this area. Food tripping in this area would be a great idea due to the abundant number of Chinese food stalls and restaurants lying in this area.

name: Manila/University Belt
summary: The University Belt, or the "U-Belt" in short, contains a large cluster of universities and colleges in Manila. The universities in this district draws locals, other Filipinos, and some foreign students. This guide only deals with the districts traditionally associated with the area, including Sampaloc, San Miguel, Santa Mesa, and the eastern fringe of Quiapo.

name: Manito
summary: Manito is a remote municipality in the southeast quadrant of Albay with coastline facing Albay Gulf and borders Sorsogon City. It is home to a boiling lake and a geothermal power plant at the foot of Pocdol Mountains.

name: Marabut
summary: Marabut is a municipality in Samar Province, Eastern Visayas, Philippines. Its coast stretches more than 20 kilometers (12 mi) along the San Pedro Bay and Leyte Gulf. In 2020, it had a population of 18,000 people.

name: Marawi
summary: Marawi is a Muslim-majority city in Lanao del Sur.

name: Marikina
summary: Marikina City known as the shoe capital of the Philippines because of the booming industry of shoe factories in the city. It is home to the world's largest pairs of shoes, and has a museum that contains collections of shoes owned by famous (and infamous) celebrities and personalities, notably that of the former first lady, Imelda Marcos.

name: Marilao
summary: Marilao is a municipality in Bulacan. Together with nearby Meycauayan, they form a large suburban area north of Metro Manila.

name: Marinduque
summary: Marinduque is an island province in the Luzon island group of the Philippines, east of Mindoro, south of Quezon Province and north of Romblon. The province, which is shaped like a heart, is often called the "Heart of the Philippines", and is the home of the Moriones Festival held during Holy Week.

name: Mariveles
summary: Mariveles is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. Situated at the southern tip of the Bataan peninsula, it is the main industrial hub of Bataan province and combines natural and historic attractions, most notably the starting point of the Bataan Death March in World War II.

name: Masbate
summary: Masbate is a largely rural island province, part of Bicol Region in the Philippines. It consists of three major islands: Masbate island proper, Ticao and Burias. It is grouped with Bicol administratively, but its local culture and languages are Visayan rather than Bicolano.

name: Masbate City
summary: Masbate City is a city of 95,000 (2015) and the capital of Masbate Province. The only city of the province, it is also a major transportation and commercial hub.

name: Masinloc
summary: Masinloc is a town of the province of Zambales in the Philippines.

name: Mati
summary: Mati is in Davao Oriental, the Philippines.

name: Matnog
summary: Matnog is the southernmost municipality of the province of Sorsogon and all of Luzon. It is at the tip of Bicol Peninsula. The town has a port going to Samar Island and vice versa.

name: Mauban
summary: Mauban (pronounced as “Ma-uban”) is a town along the Pacific coast of Quezon province, Philippines. Long isolated from the rest of the province, it has an extensive territory containing less-visited forests, waterfalls, islands, beaches and even heritage structures.

name: Mayon
summary: Mayon is an active stratovolcano with a nearly perfect cone in the province of Albay in the Philippines. It is the centerpiece of the Mayon Volcano Natural Park, one of the first national parks of the country.

name: Mayoyao
summary: Mayoyao, also known as Mayaoyao, is a town in Ifugao, a province in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. It has some of the famous Rice Terraces of the Cordilleras inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List.

name: Metro Batangas
summary: Metro Batangas is a minor metropolitan area of the Philippines, in Batangas province. The area contains 23% of the provincial population, and is a commercial, industrial and educational center. The area is entirely coastal, and houses Batangas Port, an important entry point to the rest of the Philippine archipelago.

name: Metro Cebu
summary: Metro Cebu is in Cebu Province in the Philippines. It is the country's second largest urban area, after Metro Manila, and the main urban center both of the province and of the larger Visayas region which forms the central third of the country. Metro Cebu has more than 60% of the total population of the province with nearly 3.2 million in the 2020 census.

name: Metro Manila
summary: Metro Manila (Filipino: Kalakhang Maynila), on the island of Luzon, is the national capital region of the Philippines.
