With a population of about 24 million people (2015), it is the smallest and most populous administrative region of the country, contributing 37% of the Philippines' GDP. It is the country's center of administration, business, education, diplomacy and entertainment, a huge metropolis with massive social contrasts which may even exceed those in Latin America, and are reflected in the contrasts of urban landscapes.

name: Mexico (Pampanga)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Mexico (disambiguation).
Mexico is a town in Pampanga, the Philippines. A satellite town of the provincial capital, San Fernando, it is one of the province's leading cultural and economic centers.

name: Meycauayan
summary: Meycauayan is a city in Bulacan, outside the limits of Metro Manila.

name: Miagao
summary: Miagao, also spelled as Miag-ao (both pronounced mee-ugh-OW) is a town in western Iloilo.

name: Mimaropa
summary: Mimaropa (from Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon and Palawan) is Region IV-B in the administrative system of the Philippines; as of the 2020 census it had a population of 3,228,558. Tourism, fishing and manufacturing all play a role in the economy, but agriculture is still the largest contributor at 42% of GDP.

name: Minalin
summary: Minalin is a town in Pampanga. It is the province's main egg producer and is home to an exquisitely carved Spanish-era church and extensive fishponds and wetlands.

name: Mindanao
summary: Mindanao is an island in the Philippines, the southernmost major island in the country and the second largest, after Luzon.

name: Mindoro
summary: Mindoro is an unspoiled island that's within easy reach from Manila. The town of Puerto Galera in Oriental Mindoro province is a popular tourist destination with many beach and entertainment facilities.

name: Minglanilla
summary: Minglanilla is a seaside town south of Cebu City; there is some local industry but it is largely a bedroom suburb. It is growing quickly; population was under 30,000 in 1970, about 77,000 in 2000, and 132,000 in the 2015 census.

name: Misamis Occidental
summary: Misamis Occidental is a province of the Philippines in Northern Mindanao.

name: Moalboal
summary: Moalboal is a small town on the south-west side of Cebu Island. The town sits at the base of a peninsula which runs north from there and has an assortment of tourist facilities — resorts, dive schools, bars and restaurants — along much of its west coast. Most of those are at Panagsama Beach, some further from town on White Beach.

name: Morong
summary: Morong is a municipality in the province of Rizal in the Philippines. The town is at the top of Morong Peninsula with shores on Laguna de Bay and is a vibrant cultural hub.

name: Morong (Bataan)
summary: Morong is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. It is a satellite town of Olongapo in neighboring Zambales, but is better known for its extensive beaches and the mothballed Bataan Nuclear Power Plant.

name: Mount Apo
summary: Mount Apo is a large stratovolcano in the island of Mindanao, the highest mountain in the Philippines. It is solfataric, well provided with vents emitting sulphurous fumes, and has a number of hot springs.

name: Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary
summary: Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Davao Oriental, Philippines.

name: Mount Kitanglad Range Natural Park
summary: Mt. Kitanglad Range Natural Park (MKRNP) is in Northern Mindanao of Philippines.

name: Mount Pulag National Park
summary: Mount Pulag (or sometimes Mount Pulog) is the third highest mountain in the Philippines. It is Luzon’s highest peak at 2,922 m above sea level. The borders between the provinces of Benguet, Ifugao, and Nueva Vizcaya meet at the mountain's peak.

name: Mountain Province
summary: Mountain Province is in the Cordillera region of Luzon in the Philippines. Formerly encompassing almost the entire Cordillera region, its rump core, located right in the middle of the Cordillera massif, is a center of indigenous Igorot culture.

name: Muntinlupa
summary: Muntinlupa is a city in Metro Manila, Philippines. Muntinlupa features two affluent business districts, Filinvest City and Ayala Alabang, but it is easy to be overwhelmed by the noisy sprawl around and miss some other hidden attractions. Just like other similar cities around Metro Manila, Muntinlupa incorporates old and new.

name: Murcia (Philippines)
summary: Murcia is a municipality in central Negros Occidental with a population of about 87,000 as of the 2020 census. It borders the capital city, Bacolod, and could be considered a suburb.

name: Nabua
summary: Nabua is a municipality in the Rinconada district of Camarines Sur, Bicol in the Philippines. According to the 2022 census it has a population of 87,690 people.

name: Naga
summary: Naga is one of the largest and most important cities in the Bicol region, being its center of almost everything. It is the center of commerce in the province of Camarines Sur, and is the core of the organized Metro Naga.

name: Naga (Cebu)
summary: Naga is a coastal city in Metro Cebu, located south of Cebu City, population 155,750 in the 2015 census. Neighbouring municipalities are Minglanilla to the north and San Fernando to the south.

name: Nagbukel
summary: Nagbukel is a town of 5,000 inhabitants in Ilocos Sur. It is an upland town on the boundary with Abra province inhabited by indigenous Tingguians and home to multiple waterfalls.

name: Nagcarlan
summary: Nagcarlan is a municipality of the Philippines in the province of Laguna. It is also one of the oldest towns in Laguna and was also a precolonial settlement. At first glance, it is a less touristy town than neighboring Liliw and relies more on its commercial location on a major road junction, but it also has some colonial structures, including the only underground cemetery in the Philippines, and cold springs that compete with those of Liliw.

name: Nagtipunan
summary: Nagtipunan is a municipality in Quirino.

name: Naic
summary: Naic (pronounced as “Na-ik”) is a town in Cavite. A coastal settlement along the shores of Manila Bay, it contains some beaches and sights of historic importance despite gradual urbanization.

name: Narra
summary: Narra is in Palawan, Philippines.

name: Narvacan
summary: Narvacan is a town in Ilocos Sur with extensive beaches, a Spanish-era church and some of the best bagnet (deep-fried pork belly) in the Ilocos Region.

name: Nasugbu
summary: Nasugbu is a municipality in western Batangas, facing the South China Sea. It is a tourist area, with luxury beach resorts along the coast, and some hidden draws like its asukareras (sugar plantations, from Spanish azucarera) and mountains.

name: Navotas
summary: Navotas City is a city in Metro Manila, known for its large seafood markets.

name: Negros
summary: Negros (pronounced: NEHG-rawss) is a large island in the Visayas, the island group that forms roughly the central third of the Philippines.

name: Negros Occidental
summary: Negros Occidental is a province occupying the north-western part of Negros. It is the fourth most populated province in the Philippines, known for its Chicken Inasal and its booming sugar industry, nicknamed The Sugar Bowl of the Philippines and home to one of the Philippines' active volcanoes, the majestic Mt. Kanlaon (also named Canlaon or Kanla-on).

name: Negros Oriental
summary: Negros Oriental is a province occupying the south-eastern part of Negros, and also includes Apo Island. The other part of Negros is the province of Negros Occidental.

name: New Washington
summary: New Washington is a municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport
summary: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (), commonly called NAIA, is the airport serving Manila, the capital of the Philippines, and its surrounding metropolitan area.

name: Northern Mindanao
summary: Northern Mindanao is a region of the Philippines.

name: Northern Samar
summary: Northern Samar is one of the three provinces of Samar Island in the Eastern Visayas region of the Philippines.

name: Northwest Laguna
summary: The northwestern portion of Laguna is a rough agglomeration of two towns and five cities sandwiched between the southwestern shores of Laguna de Bay and the boundary with Cavite and Batangas. With the exception of Bay and Los Baños, it is the industrial hub of Laguna and part of the urban conglomeration extending from Metro Manila.

name: Norzagaray
summary: Norzagaray, commonly shortened into Garay, is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. Located at the foothills of the Sierra Madre, it is a town that features natural attractions and civic monuments.

name: Noveleta
summary: Noveleta is a town in the western coast of Cavite. It lies to the west of Kawit (and formerly part of it) and has the junction to Cavite City to the north.

name: Nueva Ecija
summary: Nueva Ecija is a province in the Central Luzon region of the Philippines.

name: Nueva Vizcaya
summary: Nueva Vizcaya is a province in the Cagayan Valley region of Luzon.

name: Numancia
summary: Numancia is a municipality of 36,000 people (2020) in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Oas
summary: Oas is a coastal municipality in the west coast of Albay placed between the city of Ligao and the municipalities of Polangui and Libon accessible via Asian Highway 26. Its shoreline faces Burias Pass.

name: Obando
summary: Obando is a town in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. Physically separated from the province by an arm of Manila Bay and an extensive river delta system, it is often treated as a suburb of Metro Manila.

name: Olango Island
summary: Olango Island is in Cebu Province, just offshore from (east of) Mactan Island and Lapu-Lapu city. It is known mainly for its wildlife sanctuary but also has some fine beaches and dive sites. The Olango Island Group includes Olango and six smaller islands nearby. The main town and main port is Santa Rosa on the west coast.

name: Olongapo
summary: Olongapo (pronounced as “Olong-gapo”, colloquially shortened as “Gapo”) is a city in Zambales, known for the Subic Bay Freeport.

name: Orani
summary: Orani is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. Situated at the eastern side of the Bataan peninsula, it has natural and historic attractions, including the only Roman Catholic basilica in Bataan.

name: Ormoc
summary: Ormoc is a city on the west side of Leyte Island, in Leyte Province.

name: Oroquieta
summary: Oroquieta is the capital of the province of Misamis Occidental, in Northern Mindanao.

name: Oslob
summary: Oslob is a small village south of Cebu City, near the southern tip of Cebu Island. It has started blossoming into a tourist stop due to whale sharks that swim close to the coast. This tourist attraction is controversial because fisherman lure them into the coast by feeding them. It is left to the reader to decide if they want to support this.

name: Ozamiz
summary: Ozamiz, known as the "Gem of the Panguil Bay" and the "Gateway to Northwestern Mindanao", is a city in Misamis Occidental in Northern Mindanao. With a population of 143,620 (2024), it is the largest city in the province.

name: Paete
summary: Paete (pronounced pai-te) is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. The town is known for its woodcarving industry.

name: Pagadian
summary: Pagadian City, known as the "Little Hong Kong of the South" for its mountainous terrain, is the capital of the province of Zamboanga del Sur and the regional center of the Zamboanga Peninsula.

name: Pagsanjan
summary: Pagsanjan is a town in Laguna province in the Philippines. The town attracts visitors wishing to explore its heritage buildings, pray at the parish church dedicated to Our Lady of Guadalupe, or visit nature-related attractions such as Pagsanjan Falls.

name: Pagudpud
summary: Pagudpud is a municipality in the province of Ilocos Norte, Philippines. It's approximately 560 km and 10 hours by land from Manila.

name: Pakil
summary: Pakil is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. The town is known for its Baroque church, the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Turumba, and its associated Turumba Festival, one of the longest and most elaborate religious celebrations in the country.

name: Palanan
summary: Palanan is a municipality on the Pacific coast of Isabela province in the northern part of the island of Luzon in the Philippines. Cut off from the rest of the country by the Sierra Madre mountains, it is one of the least explored areas of the province, but is being geared as its future beach tourism destination.

name: Palawan
summary: Palawan is the westernmost province of the Philippines, with probably the most pristine natural environment away from its settlements. It is regularly voted among the most beautiful islands on Earth.

name: Palo
summary: Palo is a municipality in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Palompon
summary: Palompon is a historic small town in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Pampanga
summary: Pampanga is a province in the Central Luzon region of the Philippines. Dubbed as the "Culinary Capital of the Philippines"; it used to host the largest American military facility outside the United States, which has been converted to a major business and tourism hub.

name: Pamplona (Camarines Sur)
summary: Pamplona is a municipality in Camarines Sur.

name: Panabo
summary: Panabo is a city in Davao Region. It is directly north of Davao City with a road distance of 33 km. It also known as the rich of bananas and pomelos.

name: Panay
summary: Panay is an island in the Philippines, the most northwesterly of the Visayas island group. It is to the northwest of the larger island of Negros, and easily accessible with a short ferry ride from Bacolod.

name: Panay (Capiz)
summary: Panay (pronounced pan-ay with an interruption in the dash) is a town in Capiz.

name: Pangasinan
summary: Pangasinan (pronounced as “pang-gasinan”) is a province in the Ilocos Region of northern Luzon, the chief island of the Philippines. Its capital is Lingayen. Being in a fertile plain with an extensive coastline, the area is known for agricultural and aquatic products like corn crops, dried fish, carabao milk, duhat wine, nipa hut roofings, tuba and other products.

name: Pangil
summary: Pangil is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. The town is known for its natural attractions and its venerated Marian image of Our Lady of O, a rare portrayal of the Virgin Mary in her pregnant state.

name: Panglao Island
summary: Panglao is an island in Bohol Province in the Philippines with world-class diving and many tourist resorts. The resorts and other tourist facilities are concentrated in the Alona Beach area, but there are some other tourist areas and beaches scattered around the rest of the island.

name: Panglao Town
summary: Panglao Town is on Panglao Island in Bohol, Philippines.

name: Pantabangan
summary: Pantabangan is a municipality in Nueva Ecija. Having been relocated after its original site was submerged by the construction of the Pantabangan Dam in the 1970s, it is now a prime glamping spot on the foothills of the Caraballo mountains and a destination for 20th century archaeology, if you can afford to wait years for the old town to reappear from the Pantabangan Reservoir.

name: Paoay
summary: Paoay (pronounced as pa-wai) is a town in Ilocos Norte. One of the most visited places in the Ilocos region, it contains the summer residence of former Philippine president and dictator Ferdinand Marcos, a lake, a desert-like stretch of sand dunes, and a UNESCO World Heritage Roman Catholic Church.

name: Paranas
summary: Paranas is a municipality in Samar Province, Eastern Visayas, Philippines. In 2020 census, it had a population of 32,000.

name: Parañaque
summary: Parañaque is a city in southern Metro Manila. It contains the Entertainment City (E-City), the Little Las Vegas of Manila containing four huge casinos, and Baclaran, a residential and commercial neighborhood containing bustling flea markets, the Baclaran Church, backpacker inns and some nightclubs.

name: Pasacao
summary: Pasacao is a municipality of the Philippines in the province of Camarines Sur.

name: Pasay
summary: Pasay is a city in Metro Manila. Just south of Manila, this city houses the Ninoy Aquino International Airport which serves the region, and the Bay City development which hosts SM Mall of Asia, also part of Manila's tourist area. Pasay displays huge contrasts, from the relative sterility of the Bay City development to the urban blight in the rest of the city. The relative lack of sights make this rather a minor destination, except for spots like SM Mall of Asia and Star City, all within the more stable Bay City area, built on land reclaimed from Manila Bay.

name: Pasig
summary: Pasig is a city on eastern Metro Manila, lending its name from the eponymous river of the same name. Once part of Rizal province, Pasig is now part of Manila's ever-expanding sprawl. Its downtown area still maintain its characteristically Filipino charm, though overshadowed by the modernity of its central business district, Ortigas Center and swamped by uncontrolled development, slums, and pollution that Manila continues to experience.

name: Passi
summary: Passi is a city of 80,000 in Iloilo. It is at the center of Panay Island, and is the only other city of Iloilo province.

name: Pateros (Philippines)
summary: Pateros is a town, the lone municipality in Metro Manila, known for its balut and duck eggs.

name: Piat
summary: Piat is a town of Cagayan province in the Philippines. It is the pilgrimage center of the province, hosting a venerated image of the Virgin Mary dating from the 17th century.

name: Pila
summary: Pila is a town in the province of Laguna in the Philippines. One of the oldest-known settlements in the country, it is famous for its colonial-era downtown, which earns it the distinction of one of a few designated heritage towns in the Philippines.

name: Pilar (Bataan)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Pilar (disambiguation).
Pilar is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines. It is best known as the location of Mount Samat National Shrine.

name: Pilar (Sorsogon)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Pilar (disambiguation).
Pilar is a municipality in the province of Sorsogon. The town is accessible via Asian Highway 26 coming from Daraga town.

name: Pili
summary: Pili is the provincial capital of Camarines Sur, and is located to the south of Naga City.

name: Pililla
summary: Pililla is a town in Rizal, Philippines. It is known for its wind farm, Mount Sembrano, and the Halayhayin cycling path.

name: Pio Duran
summary: Pio Duran is a municipality of the Philippines in the southwest quadrant of Albay and is adjacent to the city of Ligao. Its coastline is facing Burias Pass and has a port going to the island province of Masbate.

name: Plaridel
summary: Plaridel is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines.

name: Polangui
summary: Polangui is a landlocked municipality of Albay in the northwest quadrant of the province and serves as the gateway via Asian Highway 26. Along with neighboring Libon, it borders the municipality of Bato, a town in Rinconada District of Camarines Sur. The town also provides a safe place to view Mayon Volcano during its perilous eruption.

name: Polillo Island
summary: Polillo Island is an island off the coast of eastern Quezon. It is composed of three municipalities, and largely rural area surrounded by rainforest.

name: Polomolok
summary: Polomolok is a town in South Cotabato, Soccsksargen. It is home of the country's largest pineapple plantation.

name: Porac
summary: Porac is a town in southwestern Pampanga, Philippines. Situated at the foot of the Mount Pinatubo massif and the Central Luzon plains, it combines cultural heritage and natural wonders within its territory, despite challenges brought by the Mount Pinatubo eruption in 1991 and encroaching urbanization from nearby Angeles.

name: Port Barton
summary: Port Barton is a small coastal village in Palawan, Philippines.

name: Pudtol
summary: Pudtol is a town in Apayao.

name: Puerto Galera
summary:
Puerto Galera is a town of 42,000 people (2020) on the northeastern coast of Mindoro Island, Philippines. Puerto Galera is a fairly small town and not remarkably interesting, but almost all visitors pass through it because it has the ferry terminal, and some come into it for other facilities such as ATMs or supermarkets. However, the main tourist destinations are two beach areas nearby:
Sabang, a barangay of Puerto Galera, east of the town
White Beach, in Barangay San Isidro, west

name: Puerto Princesa
summary: Puerto Princesa is the capital of the island province of Palawan. The city has been acclaimed several times as the cleanest and greenest city in the Philippines. With a wide range of attractions ranging from beaches to wildlife reserves, Puerto Princesa is a nature lover's paradise.

name: Pulilan
summary: Pulilan is a municipality (or town) in Bulacan, Philippines. It is famed for its annual Carabao Festival.

name: Quezon (Palawan)
summary: Quezon is a 2nd class municipality in the province of Palawan, Philippines. According to the 2000 census, it has a population of 41,669 people in 8,453 households. It is where the Tabon Man lived long time ago in the Philippines.

name: Quezon (province)
summary: Often called Quezon Province to distinguish it from Quezon City, Quezon is a province in Calabarzon which is rich in culture and nature. It has a bad reputation as a rainforest backwater along the highway to Bicol, but its festivals, hidden beaches, and historical monuments are things worth visiting.

name: Quezon City
summary: Quezon City (Tagalog: Lungsod Quezon) is the largest city in the Philippines and is one of the constituent cities of Metro Manila. Commonly called QC or Kyusi, it has a population of almost 3 million people in 2020. It has become the hub of information technology and its entertainment industry in the Philippines. Quezon City is a city of contrasts, mixing old and new, rich and poor, and traditional and modern.

name: Quezon City/Cubao
summary: Cubao is the commercial heart of Quezon City, at the intersection of EDSA and Aurora Boulevard. While long overshadowed by North EDSA with its large malls, the districts's status as the traditional shopping center of Quezon City refuses to die; the Araneta family, who owns Araneta City, has begun a redevelopment project for the area to return it to its former glory.

name: Quezon City/Diliman and Katipunan
summary: Diliman and Katipunan Avenue are the two university towns of Quezon City, housing two major rivalling universities, the University of the Philippines Diliman and the Ateneo de Manila University.

name: Quezon City/Northern Quezon City
summary: Commonwealth Avenue is Quezon City's second major thoroughfare, with its notorious traffic and contrasting areas, with a mix of opulence and poverty. Lying to the north of the Commonwealth Area is Fairview and Lagro areas, both mid-class communities to the north, centered on three malls facing each other along Quirino Highway. This article also covers Pasong Putik, and the Balintawak, Novaliches, Project 8, and Project 9 areas in northwestern Quezon City.

name: Quezon City/Southeast
summary: Southeast Quezon City, despite being primarily residential, has much to offer for those passing by.

name: Quezon City/Triangle and Scout Areas
summary: The Triangle Area and Scout Area of Quezon City forms the heart of the city's government center, entertainment industry, and nightlife. On the four avenues forming the Triangle Area, you may either find yourself in a row of government offices, shopping malls, residential areas, and commercial strips.

name: Quezon City/West
summary: The western parts of Quezon City is mostly a suburban residential area lying west of the Scout Area, along Quezon Avenue. While this is mostly dismissed as part of the city's sprawling environment, it does have spots worth visiting such as the Chinatown around Banawe Street, the lechon (roast pig) restaurants of La Loma, and the haunted Balete Road.

name: Quezon Memorial Circle
summary: The Quezon Memorial Circle is a national park and shrine in Quezon City, Metro Manila, Philippines.

name: Quirino
summary: Quirino is a province in the Cagayan Valley region of Luzon. One of the country's least-known provinces, it has underrated natural and cultural attractions such as indigenous communities and unspoiled mountains, rapids, caves and waterfalls.

name: Rapu-Rapu
summary: Rapu-Rapu, the only island municipality in Albay, is a tranquil "hidden gem" featuring breathtaking natural attractions, including stunning rock formations, pristine beaches, and panoramic views of Mayon Volcano with a coastline facing Albay Gulf. The town comprises three islands: Rapu-rapu Island, Batan Island, and Guinanayan Island.

name: Rizal
summary: The province of Rizal is the "R" in Calabarzon. It is a province to the east of Metro Manila with boundaries of the westernmost towns and cities of Cainta and Taytay blurring into the city of Pasig in the capital region. While becoming increasingly urbanized in the past few decades, it holds some rich secrets in both cultures and sights that are untouched by heavy and popular tourism yet are beauties of their own to be enjoyed.

name: Rizal (Cagayan)
summary: Rizal is a town of Cagayan province in the Philippines.

name: Rodriguez
summary: Rodriguez is a town at the foothills of the Sierra Madre at the province of Rizal.

name: Romblon
summary: Romblon is an archipelago province of the Philippines. It is located in the middle of the small Sibuyan Sea which separates Luzon from the Visayas.

name: Rosario (Cavite)
summary:
For Rosario of Argentina, see Rosario.
Rosario is a town in the northern coast of Cavite.

name: Roxas (Mindoro)
summary: Roxas is a town, a seaport in southern Mindoro.

name: Roxas (Palawan)
summary: Roxas (pronounced RAW-hahss) is a municipality (town) on the east coast of Palawan, north of Puerto Princesa.

name: Roxas City
summary: Roxas City is the capital city of Capiz, known for its wide seafood markets.

name: Sabang (Mindoro)
summary: Sabang is a small town located on the northeastern coast of Mindoro Island, Philippines, and administratively part of Puerto Galera.

name: Sabang (Palawan)
summary: Sabang is a small village in Palawan, Philippines. It is used as an entry point to the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River. There's not much in the village except services for those going to visit the river, but there is a beach and a chilled out atmosphere.

name: Sabtang
summary: Sabtang is an island municipality of Batanes province in the northern Philippines. It is famous for its villages composed of traditional Ivatan stone houses that form the stereotypical postcard images of the province.

name: Sagada
summary: Sagada is a small town in the Mountain Province of Luzon, Philippines. It is famous for its beautiful caves, hanging coffins, and the serene mountains.

name: Sagay
summary: Sagay is a city of 146,000 people (2015) in Negros Occidental. It is near the Sagay Marine Reserve, the largest marine reserve in the Philippines. It is known for its Sinigayan Festival, held in March.

name: Saguday
summary: Saguday is a municipality in Quirino.

name: Sagñay
summary: Sagñay is a municipality in Partido District of Camarines Sur that borders the town of Tiwi of Albay province. Its coastline is facing Lagonoy Gulf.

name: Samal
summary: Samal, formally known as Island Garden City of Samal is a city in Davao del Norte, is made up of Samal Island and the smaller Talikud Island in the Davao Gulf, making it a part of Mindanao island group. It is part of the Metropolitan Davao area and is 2 km away from Davao City, the largest city and the primary economic center of Mindanao.

name: Samal (Bataan)
summary: Samal is a town in Bataan, Central Luzon, the Philippines.

name: Samar Island
summary: Samar is the third largest island in the Philippines, after Mindanao and Luzon islands. It is located next to Leyte Island and the two are joined by a bridge.

name: Samar Province
summary: Samar, sometimes unofficially called Western Samar, is one of the three provinces in Samar Island, Eastern Visayas region of the Philippines.

name: San Antonio (Zambales)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see San Antonio (disambiguation).
San Antonio is a town of the province of Zambales in the Philippines. Situated at the western side of the mountainous Subic Peninsula, it is primarily known for its numerous secluded coves and beaches.

name: San Carlos (Negros Occidental)
summary: San Carlos is in Negros Occidental. Although the province name translates as Western Negros, this city is actually on the east coast of the island.

name: San Carlos (Pangasinan)
summary: San Carlos is in Pangasinan, Philippines.

name: San Dionisio
summary: San Dionisio is part of Iloilo.

name: San Esteban
summary: San Esteban is a town in Ilocos Sur with extensive beaches and a Spanish-era watchtower.

name: San Fabian
summary: San Fabian is a town in Pangasinan.

name: San Fernando (Cebu)
summary: San Fernando is a municipality which is part of Metro Cebu, on the coast south of Cebu City.

name: San Fernando (La Union)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see San Fernando (disambiguation).
San Fernando is a city, the capital of the province of La Union in the Philippines. It is sometimes referred to with the initials of La Union's name, L.U. (as "San Fernando, L.U."), to distinguish it from the capital city of Pampanga of the same name.

name: San Fernando (Pampanga)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see San Fernando (disambiguation).
San Fernando, sometimes referred to in short as CSF or SFDO, is a city and capital of the province of Pampanga, known as the Christmas Capital of the Philippines.

name: San Gabriel (La Union)
summary: San Gabriel is a town in La Union.

name: San Jose (Batangas)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Jose.
San Jose is a rural, agricultural municipality between Lipa and Batangas City, in Batangas.

name: San Jose (Camarines Sur)
summary: San Jose is a rural municipality of 40,000 in the province of Camarines Sur in the Philippines

name: San Jose (Mindoro)
summary: San Jose is a municipality in Occidental Mindoro, Philippines. San Jose offers an off-the-beaten-path charm for tourists who shun the crowded and over-commercialized spots in the country. The major attractions of San Jose are its three offshore islands - Ambulong, Ilin, and White Island (also called Manadi). San Jose is also a favorite jump-off point to the world-class diving site - Apo Reef Marine Park.

name: San Jose (Nueva Ecija)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Jose.
San Jose, often called San Jose City or SJC in short, is a small city in Nueva Ecija.

name: San Jose (Palawan)
summary: San Jose is a city in Palawan, Philippines.

name: San Jose de Buenavista
summary: San Jose de Buenavista, or simply San Jose, is a town of 63,000 and the capital of Antique province in the Philippines, on Panay island.

name: San Jose del Monte
summary: San Jose del Monte City, also known by its initials SJDM, is the largest city in Bulacan by population. A suburb of Metro Manila, it may look gritty at times, but has its own attractions and resorts.

name: San Juan (Batangas)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Juan (disambiguation).
San Juan is a municipality of Batangas. It is home to the other beaches in the province besides those in the west coast and Mabini;

name: San Juan (Ilocos Sur)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Juan (disambiguation).
San Juan is a coastal town in Ilocos Sur.

name: San Juan (La Union)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Juan (disambiguation).
San Juan is a town in La Union.

name: San Juan (Metro Manila)
summary: San Juan is a small city in Metro Manila, surrounded by Manila, Mandaluyong and Quezon City.

name: San Luis (Batangas)
summary: San Luis is a municipality, including the town of San Luis and some rural areas, south of Taal in Batangas. . Its main attraction is beaches.

name: San Luis (Pampanga)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Luis.
San Luis is a town in Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet agricultural town bypassed by the province's major highways.

name: San Mateo (Rizal)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see San Mateo.
San Mateo is a town in Rizal, Philippines. It is considered the gateway to the northern part of the province.

name: San Miguel (Bulacan)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Miguel.
San Miguel is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. A rural town in the middle of the Central Luzon plains, it counts heritage structures, extensive national parks and dairy-based candy-makers among its tourist draws.

name: San Pablo (Laguna)
summary:
For other places by the name, see San Pablo (disambiguation).
San Pablo is a city in the province of Laguna, known for its seven lakes.

name: San Pedro (Laguna)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see San Pedro (disambiguation).
San Pedro is a city just south of Metro Manila. The city is largely a bedroom community, serving as an important terminus for city buses toward Metro Manila, but there are also local industries. The city's tourist draws include the Sampaguita Festival, the Santo Sepulcro Parish, and the challenging KC Filipinas Golf Club.

name: San Remigio (Cebu)
summary: San Remigio is a municipality in Cebu Province, on the northwest side of Cebu Island. It has the longest coastline on the island and is an entry point to Bantayan Island via its Hagnaya Port.

name: San Teodoro (Mindoro)
summary: San Teodoro is a municipality in Oriental Mindoro. It's a quiet place, out of the way of the bustling night-life and commerce of Puerto Galera and Sabang.

name: San Vicente
summary: San Vicente is a small (34,000 in 2020) town in Palawan. It has a very fine beach 14 km (almost nine miles) long and, as of early 2015, is undergoing fairly extensive infrastructure development. Once the airport and some resorts open, it may become a major tourist destination.

name: Santa
summary: Santa is a town in Ilocos Sur.

name: Santa Ana (Philippines)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Santa Ana.
Santa Ana is a municipality in Cagayan on Luzon, the Philippines. The main beach destination in Cagayan Valley, it also hosts a freeport and is the setting of several overseas survival television series.

name: Santa Cruz (Laguna)
summary: For other cities by the name, see Santa Cruz (disambiguation).

name: Santa Cruz (Marinduque)
summary: Santa Cruz is a municipality in the province of Marinduque in the Philippines.

name: Santa Fe (Nueva Vizcaya)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Santa Fe.
Santa Fe is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated at the base of two mountain passes, it is the main point of entry leading to the Cagayan Valley region from Metro Manila by road.

name: Santa Maria (Bulacan)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see Santa Maria.
Santa Maria is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. It is a growing commercial hub in the Bulacan plains that is gradually becoming a commuter town of Metro Manila.

name: Santa Maria (Ilocos Sur)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see Santa Maria.
Santa Maria is a town in Ilocos Sur with extensive beaches, a UNESCO World Heritage-designated Spanish-era church and a towering waterfall.

name: Santa Rita
summary: Santa Rita is a town in southwestern Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet agricultural town bypassed by the province's major highways.

name: Santa Rosa (Laguna)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Santa Rosa.
Santa Rosa is a city in Laguna, a light industrial and commercial hub close to Metro Manila. Major tourist draws are the Enchanted Kingdom theme park, the Nuvali mixed-use development, and shopping spots like SM City Santa Rosa and Paseo de Santa Rosa. Santa Rosa is a major stopover for travelers to Tagaytay via Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road (Route 420).

name: Santander (Cebu)
summary: Santander is the southernmost municipality in Cebu Province, 137 km from Cebu City. It does not attract many tourists on its own merits, though there are some beach resorts. It does get quite a few travellers passing through, mostly because it has a ferry terminal that is on the main bus route between Dumaguete and Metro Cebu.

name: Santiago (Ilocos Sur)
summary:
For other cities by the name, see Santiago (disambiguation).
Santiago is a town in Ilocos Sur with extensive beaches and a Spanish-era watchtower.

name: Santiago City
summary: For Santiago of Chile, see Santiago. For other cities by the name, see Santiago (disambiguation).

name: Santo Domingo (Ilocos Sur)
summary: Santo Domingo is a coastal town in Ilocos Sur.

name: Santo Domingo (Philippines)
summary: Santo Domingo is a municipality of the Philippines in the east coast of Albay province, flanked by the provincial capital, Legazpi and the municipality of Bacacay accessible via Legazpi-Tiwi coastal road. Resorts along the town's coastline offer a wonderful view of the black beach and is on the Albay Gulf often frequented by whale sharks. It is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Santo Tomas (Batangas)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Santo Tomas.
Santo Tomas is a city in Batangas. It is the main gateway to Batangas from Manila, and is a growing industrial and commercial center.

name: Santol
summary: Santol is a town in La Union.

name: Sariaya
summary: Sariaya is a town in western Quezon. Along with neighboring Tayabas, it houses many Spanish-era cultural monuments and is nicknamed the "Heritage Capital of Quezon". Its seaside is filled with resorts, continuing from those in San Juan in Batangas.

name: Sasmuan
summary: Sasmuan is a town in southwestern Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet fishing town with extensive wetlands bypassed by the province's major highways.

name: Siargao
summary: Siargao is an island off the coast of Mindanao in the Philippines known globally as the country's surfing capital. It is composed of eight municipalities of Surigao del Norte province, but it is treated here as one destination.

name: Siaton
summary: Siaton is a municipality at the southern tip of Negros Island, in Negros Oriental Province, Philippines. Population was about 83,000 in the 2020 census.

name: Sibonga
summary: Sibonga is a municipality in Cebu Province. Population was about 48,000 in the 2015 census.

name: Sigay
summary: Sigay is a municipality in Ilocos Sur. Situated within the Cordillera mountains, it is home to the tallest waterfall in the Ilocos Region.

name: Silang
summary: Silang is a rural municipality in Cavite, along Aguinaldo Highway. It shares a mildly cool climate with its southern neighbor, Tagaytay, but is somewhat off the beaten track.

name: Silay
summary: Silay City is dubbed as the Paris of Negros because of its European-inspired houses which have been declared historical landmarks, and it is the second museum city in the Philippines next to Vigan. Silay is a center for arts, culture and ecotourism and might be as close as the province can get to the dazzling streets of Europe because of its well-preserved European colonial houses.

name: Simunul
summary: Simunul is a coastal municipality in the island province of Tawi-Tawi in Bangsamoro. It is home to some relics of what is believed to be the first mosque in the Philippines, the Sheik Karimul Makhdum Mosque, mostly built in the 1960s.

name: Sinait
summary: Sinait is a town in Ilocos Sur. Situated at the boundary with Ilocos Norte province, it is a pilgrimage spot for one of the most venerated images of the Jesus Christ in the Ilocos Region.

name: Sipalay
summary: Sipalay is a city in Negros Occidental. Population, including rural areas administered as part of the township, is around 70 thousand.

name: Sipocot
summary: Sipocot is a municipality of Camarines Sur. It is one of the most populous municipalities in the province and plays a significant role in the socio-economic development of northern Camarines Sur.

name: Siquijor
summary: Siquijor is a small island province in the Visayas lying some 22 km east of Southern Negros. While the coastline is mostly white sand beaches fronting the ocean full of tropical marine life, the interior is mountainous.

name: Sison
summary: Sison is a municipality in Pangasinan, Philippines. It's also known as "Bagoong Making" and "Salt Making" in the Philippines. Sison is part of the Region I-Ilocos Region.

name: Soccsksargen
summary: SOCCSKSARGEN (pronounced socks-sarjen), also officially known as Region XII, is a region in central Mindanao.

name: Socorro (Surigao del Norte)
summary: Socorro is an island town in Caraga Region. The whole town covers Bucas Grande Island, south of Siargao.

name: Sogod
summary: Sogod is a municipality in Southern Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Solano (Nueva Vizcaya)
summary: Solano is the largest town in Nueva Vizcaya. It is a major commercial center, a boom town, and a major stopover on the way from Manila going to Banaue or Tuguegarao.

name: Sorsogon
summary: Sorsogon just south of Albay, is the southernmost province in the island of Luzon and at the tip of Bicol Peninsula.

name: Sorsogon City
summary: Sorsogon City is the capital city of Sorsogon Province. There is little of interest here for travellers but this city may serve as a stop or a starting point for exploring beautiful Sorsogon province.

name: South Cotabato
summary: South Cotabato is a province in Soccsksargen. It is known for its tuna and pineapple industries. It is home of Mount Matutum and Lake Sebu.

name: Southern Laguna
summary: The southern portion of Laguna is a rough agglomeration of six towns and one city sandwiched between the southern shores of Laguna de Bay and the Southern Luzon Volcanic Field, a chain of inactive volcanoes running along the boundary with Batangas and Quezon provinces. Its position in the middle part of the province allows visitors to see the boundary between the urban comforts of the encroaching agglomeration from Metro Manila from the west and the rustic attractions of the towns in its eastern side.

name: Southern Nueva Vizcaya
summary: The southern portion of Nueva Vizcaya is a rough agglomeration of small towns and two protected areas around the rugged and heavily forested Cordillera and Caraballo Mountains, which cross into Nueva Ecija to the south. It has the Dalton Pass, the road gateway to Cagayan Valley.

name: Southwest Pampanga
summary: Southwest Pampanga, administratively the 2nd District, is composed of seven municipalities (and their town centers) of the province of Pampanga. They are to the west of San Fernando, the provincial capital.

name: Sual
summary: Sual is a municipality in Pangasinan.

name: Subic
summary: Subic is a municipality in Zambales Province. It shares the eponymous bay with its more famous and bustling neighbor, Olongapo, but has its own share of beach-related and natural attractions.

name: Sugpon
summary: Sugpon is a municipality in Ilocos Sur.

name: Sulu Islands
summary: The Sulu Islands are a region of the Philippines, an island chain that stretches from near Zamboanga City, at the southwestern tip of Mindanao, almost to the Malaysian province of Sabah, at the eastern end of Borneo. Politically, they are part of the Philippines but culturally they are close to Malaysia and Indonesia; in particular they are almost entirely Muslim.

name: Surigao
summary: Surigao is a city in Caraga Region of Philippine island of Mindanao.

name: Suyo
summary: Suyo is a municipality in Ilocos Sur.

name: Taal
summary: Taal is a municipality in Batangas. The old downtown (Poblacion) is noted for its Spanish colonial architecture, and is designated as a National Historical Landmark by the Philippine government.

name: Taal Volcano
summary: Taal Volcano is an active complex stratovolcano in the province of Batangas, Philippines, on an island in Taal Lake. It is one of the provincial symbols of Batangas, appearing on the new provincial seal and flag.

name: Tabaco
summary: Tabaco is a port city in the east coast of Albay, where the ferries to Catanduanes depart and is a young city having only given that status in 2001. Mayon Skyline is the main tourist attraction and it has a traditional industry of blacksmithing. Lies between the municipality of Malilipot on the south and the municipality of Malinao on the north, this city is accessible from the capital Legazpi via Legazpi-Tiwi Coastal Road. Its shoreline is facing Lagonoy Gulf and is one of the three cities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

name: Tablas
summary: Tablas Island is a diverse destination located in the province of Romblon, Philippines. Known for its stunning natural landscapes, pristine beaches, and rich cultural heritage, Tablas Island offers a delightful experience for travelers seeking a tranquil getaway.

name: Tabuk (Kalinga)
summary: Tabuk is the capital city of Kalinga province, in the Luzon Cordilleras. It is known for its whitewater rafting.

name: Tacloban
summary: Tacloban is a city in Eastern Visayas and the capital of the province of Leyte. It's the home of the Pintados Festival, a cultural event in Leyte commemorating the life and culture of the early settlers of Tacloban.

name: Tacurong
summary: Tacurong is a city in the province of Sultan Kudarat, Philippines.

name: Tagaytay
summary: Located at a mountain ridge on southern Cavite, the city of Tagaytay provides a mildly cool refuge from Manila's gritty side. It is the unofficial "Second Summer Capital" of the Philippines (the first is Baguio), and its proximity to Metro Manila draws local and foreign tourists alike. Despite the city's association with scenic Taal Volcano and the lake surrounding it, being in neighboring Batangas province, Tagaytay has many hidden things beyond the first impressions. Once a sleepy mountain town, Tagaytay has been a home to many things worth visiting: scenic viewpoints, religious sites, dining, and a new arrival, shopping malls.

name: Tagbilaran
summary: Tagbilaran is the capital city of the island province of Bohol in the Philippines. With about 105,000 residents as of 2020, it is the main point of entry to Bohol and serves as the province's political, social and economic center. Besides, it's known as the "City of Friendship".

name: Tagudin
summary: Tagudin, a town at the boundary with La Union province, is the gateway to Ilocos Sur province.

name: Taguig
summary: Taguig is a city, part of Metro Manila in the Philippines. Taguig contains the Bonifacio Global City (popularly known simply as BGC), Metro Manila's second most important business district and a major tourism, shopping, dining and entertainment destination. Other attractions include the Manila American Cemetery and the affluent neighbourhood of McKinley Hill.

name: Tagum
summary: Tagum is the capital city of the province of Davao del Norte in the Davao Region of the Philippines.

name: Talisay (Cebu)
summary: Talisay (Cebu) is a town in Metro Cebu, just south of Cebu City and bordering it.

name: Tanauan (Batangas)
summary: Tanauan is a city in Batangas, Philippines

name: Tanauan (Leyte)
summary: Tanauan is a municipality in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, Philippines.

name: Tanay
summary: Tanay is a town in Rizal, Philippines. The northern portion of the town lies within the Sierra Madre mountains.

name: Tandag
summary: Tandag is in Surigao del Sur, Caraga Region, Mindanao island.

name: Tangalan
summary: Tangalan is a municipality in the province of Aklan, Philippines.

name: Tangub
summary: Tangub is a city in of province of Misamis Occidental, in Northern Mindanao. It is best known for its month-long Christmas displays every December, and as such, it was nicknamed the "Christmas Symbol Capital of the Philippines".

name: Tanza
summary: Tanza is a town in Cavite. A coastal settlement along the shores of Manila Bay, it is at the limit of the urban sprawl of northern Cavite and contains some beaches and sights of historic importance.

name: Tarlac
summary: Tarlac is a province in Central Luzon. Tarlac is best known for its fine foods and vast sugar and rice plantations, and its fine cooking scene is due to its position as the crossroads of four major cultures. It offers some of the best cuisines from the places of ancestry of its settlers, the provinces of Pampanga, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Zambales, Pangasinan, and the Ilocos Region.

name: Tarlac City
summary: Tarlac City is the provincial capital of Tarlac. While it is the economic and educational center of Tarlac, it is a rather small provincial city, with little in the way of sights, and is more of a stopover for long-distance buses.

name: Tayabas
summary: Tayabas is the former provincial capital of Quezon. The city is home to much Spanish-era architecture, including historic ancestral houses and stone bridges.

name: Taytay (Palawan)
summary: Taytay is a municipality on the island of Palawan in the Philippines.

name: Taytay (Rizal)
summary: Taytay is a town in Rizal, Philippines. It is nicknamed the "Garment Capital of the Philippines" due to the thriving garments industry in the town and the presence of a tiangge within the town proper.

name: Tayug
summary: Tayug is an agricultural municipality producing commercial crops, livestock, and poultry in Pangasinan.

name: Teresa
summary: Teresa is a municipality of Rizal in the Philippines. This town serves as a quieter alternative to nearby urban areas.

name: Ternate (Cavite)
summary:
For other places by the name, see Ternate (disambiguation).
Ternate is a municipality in Cavite, at the boundary with Batangas. Its name derives from the island of Ternate, one of the Spice Islands (present day Maluku in Indonesia). Some of the Christianized natives from that island settled here after volunteering with the Spanish, who immediately left their garrison on Ternate.

name: Tiaong
summary: Tiaong (pronounced as “CHAH-ong”) is a town in western Quezon. It is the gateway to the province and is a primarily agricultural town with a few natural and man-made attractions in between.

name: Tigaon
summary: Tigaon is a semi urban-rural municipality of 61,000 in the Partido district of Camarines Sur. It is a rural area, with a compact town, and is known for Mount Isarog. Tigaon's coast has a beach, which still has a few resorts.

name: Tiwi
summary: Tiwi is a municipality in the northeast quadrant of Albay, Philippines at the endpoint of Legazpi-Tiwi coastal road and borders the municipality of Sagñay in Camarines Sur's Partido District. Being a neighboring municipality of Malinao, its shoreline is facing Lagonoy Gulf. It is known for its pottery industry and the geothermal power plant at the foot of Mount Malinao.

name: Toledo (Cebu)
summary: Toledo is a city on the west coast of Cebu Island.

name: Trece Martires
summary: Trece Martires, or Trece in short, is a city in Cavite in the Philippines and the de facto capital of the province. The city lacks almost anything of tourist importance, but it is a major point for travellers to the inland of southern Cavite.

name: Tuao
summary: Tuao is a town of Cagayan province in the Philippines.

name: Tuba (Benguet)
summary:
For the city in Arizona, see Tuba.
Tuba is a municipality in the province of Benguet, Philippines.

name: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
summary: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a Philippines national park, administratively in Palawan province, but geographically out in the middle of the Sulu Sea. It is regarded as one of the world's finest diving destinations, either snorkelling or SCUBA.

name: Tubigon
summary: Tubigon is a municipality on the northwest coast of Bohol, Philippines.

name: Tuguegarao
summary: Tuguegarao (pronounced as "tu-ge-garao" and commonly shortened as Tugue) is the only city in Cagayan province, and is the transportation hub for the region. It is the regional center of Cagayan Valley, with a reputation for hot weather.

name: Tumauini
summary: Tumauini is a municipality in Isabela. It is to the north of the provincial capital, Ilagan.

name: Ubay
summary: Ubay is a small town on the island province of Bohol in the Philippines.

name: Umingan
summary: Umingan (pronounced "oo-meeng-gan") is a town in Pangasinan. It is a rising eco-tourism destination ideal for nature lovers and adventurers seeking a quiet countryside escape. There are waterfalls and hot springs nearby.

name: Urdaneta
summary: Urdaneta is a city of 132,000 in Pangasinan, Philippines. It has a junction to Dagupan from the MacArthur Highway, which becomes the Manila North Road north from here. Urdaneta has some nice hotels, 3 malls and several public markets, and is the commercial center of eastern Pangasinan. It is a very nice and friendly city.

name: Uyugan
summary: Uyugan is a municipality of Batanes province in the northern Philippines.

name: Valencia (Bukidnon)
summary: Valencia is a city and provincial capital of Bukidnon in Northern Mindanao.

name: Valenzuela
summary: Valenzuela is a city of 620,000 (2015) in northwest Metro Manila. It is one of the cities forming the Camanava Area, largely a residential and industrial suburb of the region.

name: Vigan
summary: Vigan is a city in Ilocos Sur, Northern Luzon. Its Spanish colonial influence in local architecture and old-world charm make it a unique city in the Philippines.

name: Virac
summary: Virac is the largest town in Catanduanes, an island province of the Philippines, the provincial capital, and the island's main transport hub.

name: Visayas
summary: The Visayas are a major island and cultural grouping in the midsection of the Philippines. Nearly every part of the region has some fine beaches along its coasts, some fine diving areas including many coral reefs teeming with life, and some interesting historic buildings, mostly from the Spanish colonial period (1560s-1890s), in the cities and some towns. Most of the larger islands have mountains near the center, most of them volcanic in origin though few are active now.

name: Western Batangas
summary: The western part of Batangas houses the province's classical beach destinations of the province and the heritage town of Taal. This region has a humid climate and is a coastal region, dotted with some mountains to the north, bordered by southern Cavite.

name: Western Visayas
summary: Western Visayas (Region VI) is an administrative region in the Visayas island group in the Philippines. It includes the island of Panay and some smaller islands near it and also the small island province of Guimaras. The world-famous beach island of Boracay is just off the northern tip of Panay.

name: White Beach (Mindoro)
summary: White Beach (Mindoro) is in Mindoro, and is administratively part of Puerto Galera. This article also covers the barangays of Minolo, San Isidro, and Aninuan.

name: Zambales
summary: Zambales is a province in the Central Luzon region of the Philippines. Central Luzon is also called Region III.

name: Zamboanga City
summary: Zamboanga City is in the Mindanao region of the Philippines. Known as the "City of Flowers" (the etymology of Zamboanga comes from the Malay word jambangan means garden of flowers), it is now one of the most important and busiest port cities in the Philippines.

name: Zamboanga Peninsula
summary: Zamboanga Peninsula is a peninsula and an administrative region on the island of Mindanao in the Philippines.

name: Zamboanga Sibugay
summary: Zamboanga Sibugay is a province in the Zamboanga Peninsula region of the island of Mindanao in the Philippines.

name: Zamboanguita
summary: Zamboanguita is a small (about 25,000) seaside town south of Dumaguete in Negros Oriental. It has a number of diving resorts and is a jumping-off spot for boat trips to nearby Apo Island.
